definition_zh: 神经学的；神经系统的；神经科检查的
definition_en: relating to the nervous system or to neurology, the medical study and treatment of it
core_image: 一张把难以看见的神经反应画成曲线的记录纸，让隐藏的故障变得可读
scene: 门诊里，医生用小锤敲膝盖，观察小腿是否自动弹起： The doctor ordered a neurological examination after the fall.
sceneCN: 这里指「神经系统的、神经科的」（第 1 个义项：与神经系统及其医学检查有关）；句意为跌倒之后，医生安排了一次神经科检查。

pos.zh: 神经系统的；与神经病学有关的

derivatives.zh: 在神经学意义上；神经方面地

senses.title: Relating to the nervous system
senses.definition: concerning the nervous system, its functions or its diseases
senses.definitionCN: 关于神经系统、其功能或疾病的
senses.example: The doctor ordered a neurological examination after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 跌倒之后，医生安排了一次神经科检查。
senses.why: The adjective marks the domain rather than the organ: it says which system the question belongs to before saying what is wrong.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记领域而非器官：它先说问题属于哪个系统，再说哪里出了问题。

senses.title: Of the discipline of neurology
senses.definition: belonging to neurology as a branch of medicine and research
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为医学与研究分支的神经病学
senses.example: The paper appears in a neurological journal.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文发表在一本神经学杂志上。
senses.why: Once a discipline has a name, its adjective also labels journals, societies and methods, not only patients.
senses.whyCN: 一门学科有了名称之后，其形容词也标记期刊、学会与方法，而不只是病人。

senses.title: Neurological examination
senses.definition: the physical tests of reflexes, sensation, coordination and strength used to assess nerves
senses.definitionCN: 通过反射、感觉、协调与力量等体检来评估神经的方式
senses.example: A neurological examination tested her reflexes and balance.
senses.exampleCN: 一次神经科检查测试了她的反射与平衡。
senses.why: The nervous system is hard to see directly, so clinicians infer its state from a standard set of observable responses.
senses.whyCN: 神经系统难以直接看见，因此临床医生靠一组可观察的标准反应来推断其状态。

senses.title: Neurological disorder
senses.definition: a disease of the brain, spinal cord or nerves that disturbs movement, feeling or thought
senses.definitionCN: 影响脑、脊髓或神经，扰乱运动、感觉或思维的疾病
senses.example: Epilepsy is a neurological disorder with many causes.
senses.exampleCN: 癫痫是一种病因多样的神经系统疾病。
senses.why: The word groups many different lesions under the system they share, which is why it is an umbrella term.
senses.whyCN: 这个词按照共同所属的系统把许多不同病灶归为一类，因此是统称。

senses.title: Neurological damage
senses.definition: harm to nerve tissue that leaves a lasting deficit in movement, sensation or cognition
senses.definitionCN: 对神经组织的损害，留下运动、感觉或认知上的持久缺陷
senses.example: The infection left neurological damage that affected her speech.
senses.exampleCN: 感染留下了神经损伤，影响了她的言语。
senses.why: Damage is described by the system it strikes because the deficit may appear far from the original injury.
senses.whyCN: 损伤按所打击的系统来描述，因为缺陷出现的位置可能远离最初的伤处。

senses.title: Neurological development
senses.titleCN: 神经发育（儿童发育语境）
senses.definition: the growth and maturing of the nervous system, especially in early childhood
senses.definitionCN: 神经系统的生长与成熟，尤指幼儿期
senses.example: Early nutrition affects neurological development in children.
senses.exampleCN: 早期营养影响儿童的神经发育。
senses.why: Development is tracked through the functions the system should acquire, so the adjective names the expected trajectory.
senses.whyCN: 发育按该系统应当获得的功用来追踪，因此这个形容词命名预期的轨迹。

senses.title: Neurological basis
senses.titleCN: 神经机制层面的（解释语境）
senses.definition: the nerve-level mechanism proposed as the explanation of a symptom or ability
senses.definitionCN: 被提出来解释某种症状或能力的神经层面机制
senses.example: The tremor has a neurological basis rather than a psychological one.
senses.exampleCN: 这种震颤有神经机制上的基础，而非心理原因。
senses.why: Here the adjective marks a level of explanation and contrasts with other possible levels such as the social or the psychological.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词标记解释层面，并与心理、社会等其他层面形成对照。

senses.title: Neurological treatment
senses.titleCN: 神经科治疗（临床处置语境）
senses.definition: medical care directed at the nervous system, such as drugs, surgery or rehabilitation
senses.definitionCN: 针对神经系统的医疗处置，如药物、手术或康复
senses.example: Neurological treatment began with drugs to control the seizures.
senses.exampleCN: 神经科治疗先用药物控制癫痫发作。
senses.why: Treatment is classified by the system it targets, so the adjective also appears in care plans and referrals.
senses.whyCN: 治疗按所针对的系统分类，因此这个形容词也出现在照护计划与转诊中。

intro.en: Neurological is neurology plus -ical. Neurology joins Greek neuron nerve and -logia study. The English word became clinical in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: neurological 由 neurology 加 -ical 构成。neurology 由希腊 neuron「神经」与 -logia「研究」合成。这个英语词在 19 世纪转为临床用语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Neuron meant sinew, cord or nerve and was the word Greek doctors used for the body's signal cords.
items.cn: neuron 意为筋、索或神经，是希腊医生指身体信号索的用词。

items.en: The ending -logia meant the study or account of something, built on logos word, reason or account.
items.cn: 词尾 -logia 意为对某物的研究或论述，建立在 logos「言词、理性、论述」之上。

items.en: New Latin formed neurologia for the study of nerves; early uses were often theoretical rather than clinical.
items.cn: 新拉丁语构成 neurologia，指对神经的研究；早期用法多偏理论而非临床。

items.en: English neurology appears in seventeenth-century medical writing, but its modern clinical sense is later.
items.cn: 英语 neurology 出现在 17 世纪医学写作中，但其现代临床义更晚。

items.en: The ending -ical, from Latin -icalis, built the adjective neurological, meaning belonging to that study.
items.cn: 词尾 -ical 来自拉丁 -icalis，构成形容词 neurological，意为属于这门研究。

items.en: Neurology became a recognised hospital specialty in the nineteenth century, and neurological spread to examinations, disorders and wards. The exact first clinical uses are uncertain.
items.cn: 神经病学在 19 世纪成为受承认的医院专科，neurological 随之扩展到检查、疾病与病房。确切的最早临床用法存疑。

note.en: The first group holds same-stem forms and near spellings; the second holds adjectives for adjacent medical or mental domains.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干形式与形近拼写；第二组是邻近医学或精神领域的形容词。

entries.definition: The discipline itself; neurological is its adjective, so the two cannot swap places.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身；neurological 是其形容词，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: A doctor who practises neurology; the adjective describes the field, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 从事神经病学的医生；形容词描述领域，而非人。

entries.definition: Relating to nephrology, the study of the kidneys; the prefix nephro- replaces neuro- and changes the organ entirely.
entries.definitionCN: 与肾脏学有关的；前缀 nephro- 取代 neuro-，器官完全不同。

entries.definition: Historically a term for nervous or anxiety-related mental disturbance; it is psychological in use, not a medical description of nerve tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 历史上指与紧张或焦虑相关的精神障碍；使用上属心理层面，并非对神经组织的医学描述。

entries.definition: Relating to nerves, though it also means anxious; neurological is the clinical and systematic counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 与神经有关的，但也表示紧张；neurological 是更临床、更系统的对应词。

entries.definition: Relating to nerves or nerve cells; neural often describes mechanisms, while neurological describes medicine and disorders.
entries.definitionCN: 与神经或神经细胞有关的；neural 常描述机制，neurological 描述医学与疾病。

entries.definition: Relating to the brain, especially the cerebrum; neurological covers brain, cord and nerves together.
entries.definitionCN: 与脑、尤指大脑有关的；neurological 涵盖脑、脊髓与神经。

entries.definition: Relating to mental illness and its treatment; it is a neighbouring field, not a synonym, because the focus is behaviour rather than nerve tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 与精神疾病及其治疗有关的；它是邻近领域而非同义词，因为焦点在行为而非神经组织。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek stems, the real clinical phrases and the real hospital split.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词干、真实的临床搭配与真实的医院分科。

normal.en: neuron + -logia + -ical: the study of nerves turned into an adjective.
normal.cn: neuron + -logia + -ical：把「对神经的研究」变成形容词。

normal.en: Neurology is the field, a neurologist is the doctor, and neurological is the adjective.
normal.cn: neurology 是领域，neurologist 是医生，neurological 是形容词。

normal.en: The fixed phrases are a ladder: examination, disorder, damage, symptoms, development, assessment.
normal.cn: 固定搭配构成一条阶梯：检查、疾病、损伤、症状、发育、评估。

normal.en: Nephrological looks almost the same but belongs to the kidneys, so the first three letters decide the organ.
normal.cn: nephrological 看起来几乎一样，却属于肾脏，因此前三个字母决定器官。

normal.en: Psychiatric and neurological are neighbouring wards, not the same ward.
normal.cn: 精神科与神经科是相邻病房，而不是同一间病房。

abstract.en: Picture a chart of tiny waves drawn from a body that cannot show its wiring directly.
abstract.cn: 想象一张由无法直接显露线路的身体画出的细微波形图。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor tapping a knee to ask the nerves a question they must answer by reflex.
abstract.cn: 想象医生敲一下膝盖，向神经提出一个只能靠反射回答的问题。

abstract.en: Picture two doors side by side, one marked nerves and one marked mind; the adjectives decide which door.
abstract.cn: 想象并排的两扇门，一扇标神经，一扇标心智；形容词决定走哪扇。

examples.en: The patient was referred for a neurological assessment.
examples.cn: 这位病人被转去做神经功能评估。

examples.en: Neurological disorders range from migraine to epilepsy.
examples.cn: 神经系统疾病的范围从偏头痛到癫痫。

examples.en: The team studies neurological development in premature infants.
examples.cn: 该团队研究早产儿的神经发育。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛柔_logic」（neurological）——研究牛一样韧的神经索的学问 → 神经学的

root: neurology（希腊 neuron「神经」+ -logia「研究」）+ -ical；英语 neurology 见于 17 世纪，现代临床义定型于 19 世纪。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses work as labels: the system, the discipline, the examination, the disorder, the damage, the development, the explanatory level and the treatment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都是标签：系统、学科、检查、疾病、损伤、发育、解释层面与治疗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a paper trace that makes hidden nerve activity readable.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张把隐藏的神经活动变得可读的记录纸。

branches.en: TWO CONTEXTS: the system in a patient, and the discipline in a journal.
branches.cn: 两种语境：病人身上的系统，以及期刊里的学科。

branches.en: BEFORE AND DURING LIFE: an examination that asks, and a development that is watched.
branches.cn: 生前与生中：提出问题的检查，以及被观察的发育。

branches.en: FAILURE: a named disorder, and the lasting damage it leaves.
branches.cn: 失效：具名的疾病，以及它留下的持久损伤。

branches.en: THE EXPLANATION LAYER: a neurological basis is contrasted with a psychological one.
branches.cn: 解释层：神经基础与心理基础形成对照。

branches.en: RESPONSE: treatment is classified by the system it aims at.
branches.cn: 回应：治疗按所针对的系统分类。

intro.en: Neurological stacks three pieces: neuron nerve, -logia study, and -ical relating to. Each can be read separately.
intro.cn: neurological 叠了三段：neuron「神经」、-logia「研究」与 -ical「与……有关的」，每一段都可单独读出。

latinIntro.en: New Latin neurologia combined Greek neuron with -logia, and Latin -icalis supplied the adjective ending; the same pieces build neurological in English.
latinIntro.cn: 新拉丁 neurologia 把希腊 neuron 与 -logia 结合，拉丁 -icalis 提供形容词词尾；同样的部件在英语中构成 neurological。

items.example: The stem names the body's signal cords.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名身体的信号索。

items.example: The suffix names a discipline.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名一门学科。

items.example: The suffix turns the discipline into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把学科变成形容词。

items.meaning: the study of the nervous system
items.example: Neurology has its own wards and journals.
items.exampleCN: 神经病学有自己的病房与期刊。

items.example: The neurological examination tested her reflexes.
items.exampleCN: 神经科检查测试了她的反射。

items.example: The neurologist reviewed the scan.
items.exampleCN: 神经科医生查看了影像。

items.example: The patient is neurologically stable.
items.exampleCN: 这位病人神经方面情况稳定。

items.example: Neuropathy causes numbness in the feet.
items.exampleCN: 神经病引起足部麻木。

items.meaning: the scientific study of the nervous system
items.example: Neuroscience combines biology, psychology and medicine.
items.exampleCN: 神经科学结合生物学、心理学与医学。

definition_zh: 神经元；神经细胞
definition_en: a cell of the nervous system that receives signals and passes them on to other nerve cells
core_image: 一个带许多触须的小节点，一头接上线，另一头把信号递出去
scene: 显微镜下，一张神经组织的图里，一个细长的节点伸出许多分支，连向四周： Each neuron sends its signal along a single long fibre.
sceneCN: 这里指「神经元」这一细胞单位（第 1 个义项：神经系统中传递信号的细胞）；句意为每个神经元沿一条长纤维把信号送出。

pos.zh: 神经元；神经细胞（神经系统的基本单元）
（人工神经网络中的）神经元单元

derivatives.zh: 神经毡（神经纤维与胶质构成的网）

senses.title: The nerve cell
senses.titleCN: 神经元：神经系统的基本细胞单位
senses.definition: a cell with a body, one or more long fibres and many branches, which receives and transmits nerve signals
senses.definitionCN: 具有胞体、一条或多条长纤维与许多分支、能接收并传导神经信号的细胞
senses.example: Each neuron sends its signal along a single long fibre.
senses.exampleCN: 每个神经元沿一条长纤维把信号送出。
senses.why: The cell is defined by its shape as much as its tissue: a compact body with a long output line is what makes point-to-point signalling possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个细胞既由组织定义，也由形状定义：紧凑的胞体加一条长输出线，才使点对点传导成为可能。

senses.title: Sensory neuron
senses.titleCN: 感觉神经元：把外界信息送进来
senses.definition: a neuron that carries signals from a sense organ or receptor toward the central nervous system
senses.definitionCN: 把来自感觉器官或感受器的信号传向中枢神经系统的神经元
senses.example: A sensory neuron reports the heat of the cup to the spinal cord.
senses.exampleCN: 感觉神经元把杯子的热度报告给脊髓。
senses.why: Direction defines this type: the signal travels inward, so the cell is named for the side it serves.
senses.whyCN: 方向定义了这一类型：信号向内走，因此这个细胞按它所服务的一端命名。

senses.title: Motor neuron
senses.titleCN: 运动神经元：把指令送出去
senses.definition: a neuron that carries signals from the central nervous system to a muscle or gland
senses.definitionCN: 把信号从中枢神经系统传到肌肉或腺体的神经元
senses.example: A motor neuron tells the hand to close around the cup.
senses.exampleCN: 运动神经元让手合拢握住杯子。
senses.why: This is the mirror image of the sensory type: the same cell structure, with the signal pointed outward.
senses.whyCN: 这是感觉型的镜像：同样的细胞结构，信号朝外指。

senses.title: Interneuron
senses.titleCN: 中间神经元：在系统内部转接
senses.definition: a neuron that connects other neurons inside the central nervous system rather than reaching the body's surface
senses.definitionCN: 在中枢神经系统内部连接其他神经元、不直接到达体表的神经元
senses.example: An interneuron passes the signal from a sensory cell to a motor cell.
senses.exampleCN: 中间神经元把信号从感觉细胞传给运动细胞。
senses.why: Most neurons neither enter nor leave the body; they sit between, which is why the name simply marks the middle position.
senses.whyCN: 大多数神经元既不进入也不离开身体，而是位于中间，因此名称只标记中间位置。

senses.title: Artificial neuron
senses.titleCN: 人工神经元：计算模型中的单元
senses.definition: a simple computing unit that takes several inputs, weights them and passes one output on
senses.definitionCN: 接收若干输入、加权后输出一个信号的简单计算单元
senses.example: Each artificial neuron adds its inputs and fires above a threshold.
senses.exampleCN: 每个人工神经元把输入相加，超过阈值就「放电」。
senses.why: The machine keeps only the input-weight-output shape of the cell, which is why the biological name was borrowed.
senses.whyCN: 机器只保留细胞「输入—加权—输出」的形状，因此借用了生物学名称。

senses.title: Anatomy of a neuron
senses.titleCN: 神经元的解剖形态（胞体、轴突、树突）
senses.definition: the parts of a nerve cell: cell body, axon and dendrites, each with a different role in signalling
senses.definitionCN: 神经细胞的组成部分：胞体、轴突与树突，各自在传导中承担不同角色
senses.example: The axon of a neuron can be longer than the whole spinal cord segment.
senses.exampleCN: 一个神经元的轴突可能比整段脊髓还长。
senses.why: Once the cell is understood as a device, its parts are named by the direction in which they pass the signal.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把细胞理解为装置，它的各部分就按传导方向命名。

senses.title: Neuron degeneration
senses.definition: the loss or wasting of nerve cells, as in several progressive diseases
senses.definitionCN: 神经细胞的丧失或萎缩，见于若干进行性疾病
senses.example: The disease slowly destroys the neurons that control walking.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疾病逐渐破坏控制行走的神经元。
senses.why: When cells are lost they are not replaced easily, so clinical talk focuses on the unit rather than the whole system.
senses.whyCN: 细胞丧失后不易补充，因此临床讨论聚焦于这一单位而非整个系统。

senses.title: The functional unit
senses.titleCN: 作为功能单元的神经元
senses.definition: the smallest unit that can receive, integrate and pass on a nerve signal
senses.definitionCN: 能接收、整合并传出神经信号的最小单位
senses.example: Physiologists treat the neuron as the functional unit of the nervous system.
senses.exampleCN: 生理学家把神经元视为神经系统的功能单位。
senses.why: A unit is defined by what it can do alone, and a single cell can take in, sum and send a signal.
senses.whyCN: 单位由它能独立完成的事定义，而单个细胞就能接收、汇总并发出信号。

intro.en: Neuron is Greek neuron, meaning sinew, cord or nerve. The modern sense of a nerve cell dates from nineteenth-century microscopy. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: neuron 即希腊语 neuron，意为筋、索或神经。指神经细胞的现代义来自 19 世纪显微解剖学。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek neuron meant sinew, cord or nerve, and it could name both the string-like structure and the bodily organ of feeling.
items.cn: 希腊 neuron 意为筋、索或神经，既可指索状结构，也可指身体的感觉器官。

items.en: Latin nervus is the cognate of neuron and supplies the rival English family nerve and nervous; the shared ancestor is reconstructed.
items.cn: 拉丁 nervus 与 neuron 同源，提供英语的另一支 nerve 与 nervous；共同祖形为重构形式。

items.en: Early anatomists used neuron for the nerve fibre or the whole cord, not yet for a single cell.
items.cn: 早期解剖学家用 neuron 指神经纤维或整条索，尚未指单个细胞。

items.en: Improved microscopes and staining showed that nerve tissue is made of discrete cells, and the cell sense of neuron took hold.
items.cn: 显微镜与染色的进步显示神经组织由离散的细胞构成，neuron 的细胞义由此确立。

items.en: The cell sense is usually credited to late nineteenth-century work, including the naming associated with Wilhelm Waldeyer in 1891; the exact first use is debated.
items.cn: 细胞义通常归功于 19 世纪后期的工作，包括 1891 年与 Wilhelm Waldeyer 相关的命名；确切的最早使用仍有争议。

items.en: Twentieth-century neuroscience added the artificial neuron and the neuron doctrine, extending the word beyond anatomy.
items.cn: 20 世纪神经科学又添人工神经元与神经元学说，把这个词扩展到解剖学之外。

note.en: The first group holds look-alike words and spelling variants; the second holds the parts and neighbours of a neuron.
note.cn: 第一组是形近词与拼写变体；第二组是神经元的部件与邻近结构。

entries.definition: A particle with no charge in an atomic nucleus; it is one letter away in sound but belongs to physics, not biology.
entries.definitionCN: 原子核中不带电的粒子；读音只差一点，却属于物理而非生物。

entries.definition: A British variant spelling of neuron; it is the same cell, not a different structure.
entries.definitionCN: neuron 的英式变体拼写；指同一个细胞，不是另一种结构。

entries.definition: Relating to nerves or nerve cells; it describes, while neuron names the cell.
entries.definitionCN: 与神经或神经细胞有关的；它作描述，neuron 命名细胞。

entries.definition: The tangled mass of fibres and glia between nerve cell bodies; it is tissue, not a single cell.
entries.definitionCN: 神经细胞体之间纤维与胶质缠结的团块；它是组织，不是单个细胞。

entries.definition: The everyday term for a neuron; it says what the cell is without using the Greek word.
entries.definitionCN: 神经元的日常说法；不用希腊词而直接说明这个细胞是什么。

entries.definition: The long fibre that carries a signal away from the cell body; it is a part of a neuron.
entries.definitionCN: 把信号从胞体带走的长纤维；它是神经元的一部分。

entries.definition: A branching fibre that receives signals and brings them toward the cell body.
entries.definitionCN: 接收信号并把信号带向胞体的分支纤维。

entries.definition: The gap or junction where one neuron passes a signal to another; it belongs to neither cell alone.
entries.definitionCN: 一个神经元把信号传给另一个的间隙或接头；它不属于任一细胞单独所有。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek cord word, the real cell doctrine and the real parts of the cell.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊索状词、真实的细胞学说与真实的细胞部件。

normal.en: Greek neuron meant cord, and a nerve cell is a tiny cord with branches.
normal.cn: 希腊 neuron 意为索，而神经细胞就是一根带分支的微小索。

normal.en: The three functional types are named by direction: sensory in, motor out, interneuron between.
normal.cn: 三种功能类型按方向命名：感觉向内、运动向外、中间神经元居中。

normal.en: Axon carries away, dendrite brings in, and the cell body sits between them.
normal.cn: 轴突带出，树突带入，胞体位于两者之间。

normal.en: An artificial neuron keeps only the shape: inputs, weights, one output.
normal.cn: 人工神经元只保留形状：输入、权重、一个输出。

normal.en: In British spelling the word can also be written neurone, with the same meaning.
normal.cn: 英式拼写也可写作 neurone，意思完全相同。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny switchboard with many incoming wires and one outgoing wire.
abstract.cn: 想象一台小交换机，许多线进来，一根线出去。

abstract.en: Picture a relay runner who receives a baton and passes it on without keeping it.
abstract.cn: 想象接力跑者，接到棒就传下去，从不把棒留在手里。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd where each person can only whisper to a neighbour, yet a message crosses the whole room.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人只能对邻座耳语，消息却能传遍整个房间。

examples.en: A single neuron can connect to thousands of others.
examples.cn: 一个神经元可以连接数千个其他神经元。

examples.en: Motor neurons weaken in the disease that gradually removes movement.
examples.cn: 在那种逐渐夺走运动能力的疾病中，运动神经元会变弱。

examples.en: The model treats each neuron as a simple weighted sum.
examples.cn: 该模型把每个神经元当作一个简单的加权求和。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛龙」（neuron）——一头牛身上布满细索，每个结都是一个细胞 → 神经元

root: 希腊 neuron「筋、索、神经」，与拉丁 nervus 同源；指单个神经细胞的现代义形成于 19 世纪显微解剖学。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe one cell: the basic unit, three directional types, the artificial unit, its anatomy, its degeneration, and finally its status as the functional unit of the system.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述同一个细胞：基本单位、三种方向类型、人工单元、解剖形态、退化损伤，最后是它作为系统功能单位的地位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small node with many feelers in and one long line out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小节点，许多触须伸进来，一条长线伸出去。

branches.en: THE CELL AND ITS PARTS: the unit as a whole, and the body, axon and dendrites that make it.
branches.cn: 细胞与部件：作为整体的单位，以及构成它的胞体、轴突与树突。

branches.en: THREE DIRECTIONS: inward, outward and between.
branches.cn: 三个方向：向内、向外与居中。

branches.en: THE MACHINE COPY: inputs, weights and one output.
branches.cn: 机器复制品：输入、权重与一个输出。

branches.en: WHEN CELLS DIE: loss of the unit removes the function.
branches.cn: 细胞死亡时：单位的丧失带走功能。

branches.en: WHY IT COUNTS AS A UNIT: it can receive, sum and send on its own.
branches.cn: 为何算作单位：它能独立完成接收、汇总与发出。

intro.en: Neuron is a Greek noun; its English family grows through the suffixes -al, -al + -ly and compounds such as neuropil.
intro.cn: neuron 是希腊名词；其英语词族经 -al、-al + -ly 与 neuropil 这类复合形式扩展。

latinIntro.en: Greek neuron entered Latin medical writing and shares a root with Latin nervus; the adjective neuronalis is a modern scientific formation.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 neuron 进入拉丁医学写作，与拉丁 nervus 共享词根；形容词 neuronalis 是现代科学构词。

items.example: The term shifted from the cord to the cell.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从「索」转到「细胞」。

items.example: Neuronal loss explains the symptoms.
items.exampleCN: 神经元丧失解释了这些症状。

items.example: The tissue was neuronally organised.
items.exampleCN: 这块组织在神经元层面是有结构的。

items.meaning: the output fibre of a neuron
items.example: The axon carries the signal away.
items.exampleCN: 轴突把信号带走。

items.example: Dendrites spread like small trees.
items.exampleCN: 树突像小树一样展开。

items.example: The synapse passes the signal across a gap.
items.exampleCN: 突触把信号送过间隙。

items.meaning: the felted fibre mass between cell bodies
items.meaningCN: 细胞体之间毡状的纤维团
items.example: Neuropil fills the spaces between neurons.
items.exampleCN: 神经毡填满神经元之间的空隙。

items.example: The marker is neuron-specific.
items.exampleCN: 这个标记是神经元特异性的。

items.meaningCN: 位于其他神经元之间的神经元
items.example: Interneurons relay signals inside the cord.
items.exampleCN: 中间神经元在脊髓内部转接信号。

definition_zh: 中立的；中性的；不带电的；空挡的；中性色的
definition_en: not taking either side in a conflict, neither acid nor alkaline, carrying no charge, or being neither one nor the other of two
core_image: 拔河绳上的红布停在两条界线正中间：两边都不到
scene: 裁判站在两名摔跤手中间，双臂下垂，不偏向任何一方。A referee stands between two wrestlers with both arms down and stays neutral, favouring neither.
sceneCN: 这里 neutral 是「不选边、不介入」（第 2 个义项：在两方冲突中不偏向任何一方）；句意：裁判站在两名摔跤手之间，双臂下垂，保持中立，不偏向任何一方。图中可辨识物件：摔跤垫、两名选手、居中站立的裁判、下垂的双臂；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Alchemical balance: opposing elements in proportion
senses.titleCN: 炼金术的平衡：对立元素按比例相抵
senses.definition: in alchemy, of a substance made from opposing elements that balance each other exactly
senses.definitionCN: 在炼金术中，指由相互对立的元素按比例恰好相抵而成的物质
senses.example: Alchemists called a body neutral when fire and water balanced in it.
senses.exampleCN: 当火与水在物体中相抵平衡时，炼金术士称该物体为 neutral。
senses.why: Neutral is first recorded in the 1540s in alchemy, where opposite qualities were thought to cancel each other. The core picture is a scale that stops exactly in the middle.
senses.whyCN: neutral 最早记录于 16 世纪 40 年代，用于炼金术，当时认为对立的性质会相互抵消。核心画面是一架恰好停在正中的天平。

senses.title: Not taking sides: outside a conflict
senses.definition: not supporting either party in a dispute, war, or argument
senses.definitionCN: 在争端、战争或争论中不支持任何一方
senses.example: The referee stayed neutral and let both sides speak.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判保持中立，让双方都把话说完了。
senses.why: The alchemical balance became a social one: two opposing sides cancel, and the person in the middle belongs to neither. This sense is recorded alongside the first.
senses.whyCN: 炼金术的平衡变成了社会的平衡：两个对立面相互抵消，中间的人不属于任何一边。这个义项与最早义项同时被记录。

senses.title: Chemistry: neither acid nor alkaline
senses.definition: of a solution, having a pH near seven, neither acidic nor basic
senses.definitionCN: 指溶液 pH 接近七，既非酸性也非碱性
senses.example: Pure water is neutral, with a pH close to seven.
senses.exampleCN: 纯水是中性的，pH 接近七。
senses.why: Chemistry took the balance image literally: acid and alkali cancel, and the middle point is neutral. The sense is recorded from the 1660s.
senses.whyCN: 化学把这个平衡意象落到实处：酸与碱相抵，中间点就是中性。该义项记录于 17 世纪 60 年代。

senses.title: Not a belligerent: outside the war
senses.titleCN: 非交战国：站在战争之外
senses.definition: of a country or ship, not belonging to either side in a war
senses.definitionCN: 指国家或船只不属于战争中的任何一方
senses.example: Neutral shipping was allowed through the blockade.
senses.exampleCN: 中立国的船只被允许通过封锁线。
senses.why: A state can hold the same position as the referee: it takes no side, so its ships and ports stay outside the fighting. The sense is recorded from 1711.
senses.whyCN: 国家可以处在和裁判相同的位置：不选边，因此它的船只与港口留在战斗之外。该义项记录于 1711 年。

senses.title: Colour: low saturation, easy to live with
senses.definition: of a colour, muted and close to grey or beige, used as a quiet base
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色柔和、接近灰或米色，用作安静的底色
senses.example: The room was painted in neutral greys and warm beiges.
senses.exampleCN: 房间刷成了中性灰和暖米色。
senses.why: A muted colour sits between the strong hues and commits to none. The balance image moves from substances to light, and the sense is recorded from 1821.
senses.whyCN: 柔和的颜色处在各种强烈色相之间，不偏向任何一种。平衡意象从物质移到光线，该义项记录于 1821 年。

senses.title: Electrical neutrality: no net charge
senses.definition: having equal positive and negative charge, so that no net charge remains
senses.definitionCN: 正负电荷相等，因此没有净电荷残留
senses.example: A neutron carries no charge and is electrically neutral.
senses.exampleCN: 中子不带电荷，是电中性的。
senses.why: Positive and negative charges cancel exactly as acid and alkali cancel. The word's balance is now counted in charge rather than in qualities.
senses.whyCN: 正负电荷的相抵，正如酸与碱的相抵。这个词的平衡现在以电荷计算，而不是以性质计算。

senses.title: A neutral party: the person or state in the middle
senses.titleCN: 中立的一方：处在中间的人或国家
senses.definition: a person, country, or place that takes no side, often chosen to host talks
senses.definitionCN: 不选边的人、国家或地点，常被选作会谈地点
senses.example: The talks were held in a neutral, far from both capitals.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈在一个远离两国首都的中立地点举行。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the party that holds the middle position. Recorded as a noun in the mid-15c., it names whoever the balance leaves uncommitted.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成名词，指占据中间位置的一方。该名词义在 15 世纪中期已有记录，命名的是被天平留在“未承诺”状态的那一方。

senses.title: Mechanical neutral: no gear engaged
senses.titleCN: 机械空挡：没有齿轮咬合
senses.definition: of a gearbox, in the position where no gear is engaged and no power reaches the wheels
senses.definitionCN: 指变速器处在没有齿轮咬合、动力不传到车轮的位置
senses.example: He shifted into neutral and let the car roll to a stop.
senses.exampleCN: 他挂入空挡，让车滑行到停下。
senses.why: In a gearbox the middle position transmits nothing: neither forward nor reverse. The sense, recorded from 1905, is the balance image in metal.
senses.whyCN: 在变速器里，中间位置什么也不传递：既不前进也不后退。该义项记录于 1905 年，是平衡意象在金属中的版本。

senses.title: Grammatical neuter: neither masculine nor feminine
senses.titleCN: 语法中性：既非阳性也非阴性
senses.definition: in grammar, of a gender that is neither masculine nor feminine
senses.definitionCN: 在语法中，指既非阳性也非阴性的性
senses.example: Latin bellum, meaning war, is a neuter noun.
senses.exampleCN: 拉丁语 bellum（战争）是一个中性名词。
senses.why: Latin neuter means 'neither the one nor the other of two'. Grammar applies that either-or refusal to gender, so a noun can stand outside the pair.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 neuter 意为“两者皆非”。语法把这种“两个都不是”的拒绝用在性上，于是名词可以站在这对选项之外。

senses.title: Neutral tone: plain and non-committal
senses.definition: of language or manner, plain and without emotion, giving nothing away
senses.definitionCN: 指语言或态度平实、不带情绪，不透露立场
senses.example: She answered in a neutral tone that gave nothing away.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一种不露声色的中性语气回答。
senses.why: A neutral colour commits to no hue, and a neutral tone commits to no side. The same middle position is applied to speech.
senses.whyCN: 中性色不对任何色相表态，中性语气也不对任何一方表态。同一个“中间位置”被用到了言语上。

intro.en: Neutral is recorded in the 1540s, first in alchemy for a balance of opposing elements, and almost at once for a person who takes no side. Latin neutralis goes back to neuter 'neither the one nor the other', probably a calque of Greek oudeteros.
intro.cn: neutral 记录于 16 世纪 40 年代，最初用于炼金术中对立元素的平衡，几乎同时就用于不选边的人。拉丁语 neutralis 可追溯至 neuter“两者皆非”，很可能是希腊语 oudeteros 的仿译。

items.en: First recorded in the 1540s in alchemy, for a substance in which opposing elements balance, and for the sense 'not taking sides'.
items.cn: 最早记录于 16 世纪 40 年代，用于炼金术中对立元素相衡的物质，同时也有“不选边”义。

items.en: By the 1550s the word is used of persons who do not join either party in a quarrel.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪 50 年代，这个词已用于不加入争吵任何一方的人。

items.en: Latin neutralis comes from neuter 'neither the one nor the other, neither of two': ne- 'not' plus uter 'either of two'. It is probably a calque of Greek oudeteros.
items.cn: 拉丁语 neutralis 来自 neuter“两者皆非、两者都不是”：ne-“不”加 uter“两者之一”。它很可能是希腊语 oudeteros 的仿译。

items.en: The two parts are PIE *ne- 'not' and the stem behind uter 'either', which is related to English whether.
items.cn: 两个部分分别是原始印欧语 *ne-“不”与 uter“两者之一”背后的词干，后者与英语 whether 同源。

items.en: Chemistry adopts the word in the 1660s for 'neither acid nor alkaline'; the sense 'not a belligerent' follows in 1711 and the colour sense in 1821.
items.cn: 化学在 17 世纪 60 年代采用这个词，表示“非酸非碱”；“非交战国”义随后于 1711 年出现，颜色义于 1821 年出现。

items.en: The noun is recorded in the mid-15c.; mechanical neutral appears in 1905, and the neutral particle the neutron takes the word into physics.
items.cn: 名词义在 15 世纪中期已有记录；机械空挡义出现于 1905 年，而中性粒子 neutron 把这个词带进了物理学。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and scientific kinship, the second for the idea of not taking a side.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写与科学上的亲缘关系挑选，第二组按“不选边”的意思挑选。

entries.definition: grammatically neither masculine nor feminine. It is the Latin source word neuter, from which neutralis was formed.
entries.definitionCN: 语法上既非阳性也非阴性的。它就是拉丁语源词 neuter，neutralis 由它构成。

entries.definition: existing in nature, not made by people. It starts from Latin natura 'birth', not from neuter.
entries.definitionCN: 自然的；天生的。它来自拉丁语 natura“出生”，不是来自 neuter。

entries.definition: a particle with no electric charge. Its name was coined from neutral plus -on.
entries.definitionCN: 不带电的粒子。它的名字由 neutral 加 -on 造出。

entries.definition: not favouring one side unfairly. It judges fairly between parties, while neutral can also mean simply staying out.
entries.definitionCN: 公正的；不偏不倚的。它在两方之间公正判断，而 neutral 也可以只是置身事外。

entries.definition: showing no interest or concern. It describes unconcern, while neutral describes a balanced position between sides.
entries.definitionCN: 漠不关心的。它描述的是不关心，而 neutral 描述的是在两方之间的平衡位置。

entries.definition: of a state, not formally allied to any major power bloc. It is a political term, narrower than neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 不结盟的。它指国家不正式加入任何大国集团，是政治术语，范围比 neutral 窄。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: ne- plus uter inside neuter, the Latin source neutralis, and the dated scientific senses that followed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：neuter 内部的 ne- 加 uter、拉丁语来源 neutralis，以及随后有年代可查的科学义项。

normal.en: ne- 'not' plus uter 'either of two' makes 'neither of the two': the middle position is built into the word.
normal.cn: ne-“不”加 uter“两者之一”就是“两者皆非”：中间位置被造进了这个词里。

normal.en: Alchemy gave the first sense, a balance of opposing elements; chemistry kept the picture as neither acid nor alkaline.
normal.cn: 炼金术给了第一个义项，即对立元素的平衡；化学保留这幅画，表示非酸非碱。

normal.en: A neutral country and a neutral referee hold the same spot: outside the two sides.
normal.cn: 中立国与中立裁判站的是同一个位置：在两方之外。

normal.en: Neutral grey commits to no hue, just as a neutral tone commits to no opinion.
normal.cn: 中性灰不对任何色相表态，正如中性语气不对任何观点表态。

normal.en: A gearbox in neutral transmits nothing: the balance image appears again in metal.
normal.cn: 处于空挡的变速器什么也不传递：平衡意象又一次出现在金属里。

abstract.en: A tug-of-war rope whose red marker hangs exactly on the centre line: both teams pull, the marker stays.
abstract.cn: 拔河绳上的红布恰好停在中心线上：两队都在拉，红布不动。

abstract.en: Two arrows pushing a ball from opposite sides with equal force: the ball does not move.
abstract.cn: 两支箭头从相反方向用同样的力推一个球：球不移动。

abstract.en: A switch resting in the middle between on and off: no current, no direction, no commitment.
abstract.cn: 一个停在“开”与“关”正中的开关：没有电流、没有方向、没有承诺。

examples.en: The mediator remained neutral even when one side raised its voice.
examples.cn: 即使一方提高了嗓门，调解人仍然保持中立。

examples.en: Choose a neutral wall colour so the furniture can change later.
examples.cn: 选一种中性的墙面颜色，以后换家具也容易搭配。

examples.en: The country declared itself neutral at the start of the war.
examples.cn: 这个国家在战争开始时宣布中立。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛戳」——牛站在两方中间，哪边都不戳、不顶 → neutral 中立的、中性的

root: 源自拉丁语 neutralis，来自 neuter“两者皆非”＝ ne-“不”＋ uter“两者之一”；uter 与 whether 同源，很可能是希腊语 oudeteros 的仿译。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of neutral all come from a single position: exactly in the middle, committed to neither side. Alchemy applied it to elements, politics to parties, chemistry to acids, physics to charge, grammar to gender, and speech to tone.
sensesIntro.cn: neutral 的十个义项都来自同一个位置：恰在正中，不属于任何一边。炼金术把它用在元素上，政治用在阵营上，化学用在酸碱上，物理用在电荷上，语法用在性上，言语用在语气上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tug-of-war marker stopped exactly on the centre line.
core.cn: 核心意象：拔河绳上的标记恰好停在中心线上。

branches.en: THE BALANCED MIDDLE: opposing elements in alchemy, and opposing parties in a dispute.
branches.cn: 平衡的中间：炼金术中的对立元素，以及争端中的对立两方。

branches.en: SCIENTIFIC NEUTRALITY: neither acid nor alkaline, and no net electric charge.
branches.cn: 科学上的中性：非酸非碱，以及净电荷为零。

branches.en: THE UNCOMMITTED PARTY: a state outside a war, and the person or place chosen to host talks.
branches.cn: 未承诺的一方：战争之外的国家，以及被选作会谈地点的人或地方。

branches.en: THE QUIET SURFACE: low-saturation colour, and a tone that gives nothing away.
branches.cn: 安静的表层：低彩度的颜色，以及不透露立场的语气。

branches.en: NEITHER ENGAGED NOR EITHER: a gearbox in neutral, and a grammatical gender outside the pair.
branches.cn: 既不咬合也不属于任何一边：空挡的变速器，以及跳出阴阳两性的语法中性。

intro.en: Neutral is Latin neutralis plus -al, from neuter. English builds neutrality, neutrally, neutralize, neutralization, neutralist and neutralism, and the same stem gives neuter and neutron.
intro.cn: neutral 是拉丁语 neutralis 加 -al，源自 neuter。英语构造出 neutrality、neutrally、neutralize、neutralization、neutralist、neutralism，同一词干还给出 neuter 与 neutron。

latinIntro.en: Latin neutralis 'of the neuter gender, neutral' comes from neuter 'neither of two', itself ne- 'not' plus uter 'either of two'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 neutralis“中性的、中立的”来自 neuter“两者皆非”，后者由 ne-“不”加 uter“两者之一”构成。

items.meaning: taking no side; neither one nor the other
items.meaningCN: 中立的；中性的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The village stayed neutral during the dispute.
items.exampleCN: 争端期间这个村子保持中立。

items.meaning: the state of taking no side
items.meaningCN: 中立；中性（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The treaty guaranteed the neutrality of the port.
items.exampleCN: 条约保障了该港口的中立地位。

items.meaningCN: 中立地；平淡地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She described the quarrel neutrally, naming no culprit.
items.exampleCN: 她中立地描述了这场争吵，没有指名任何一方。

items.meaning: to cancel the effect of something
items.meaningCN: 使中和；抵消（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The base neutralizes the acid almost instantly.
items.exampleCN: 碱几乎立刻中和了酸。

items.meaning: the act of cancelling or balancing
items.meaningCN: 中和作用；抵消（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: The neutralization produced ordinary salt and water.
items.exampleCN: 中和反应生成了普通的盐和水。

items.meaningCN: 中立主义者（-ist 构成人名名词）
items.example: The neutralists opposed joining either alliance.
items.exampleCN: 中立主义者反对加入任何一个联盟。

items.meaning: the policy of staying outside rival blocs
items.meaningCN: 中立主义（-ism 构成主张名词）
items.example: Neutralism shaped the country's foreign policy.
items.exampleCN: 中立主义塑造了该国的外交政策。

items.meaningCN: 中性的；既非阳也非阴（ne-“不”+ uter“两者之一”）
items.example: The Latin word for leaf is neuter.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语中“叶子”这个词是中性名词。

items.meaning: a particle with no electric charge
items.meaningCN: 中子（neutral 加粒子后缀 -on，指不带电的粒子）
items.example: A neutron passes through the electric field undeflected.
items.exampleCN: 中子穿过电场时不发生偏转。

items.meaningCN: 中和剂；抵消物（-er 构成施动物名词）
items.example: The lab keeps a neutralizer beside every acid bath.
items.exampleCN: 实验室在每个酸槽旁都放一瓶中和剂。

latinEntries.meaning: neither the one nor the other

latinEntries.meaningCN: 两者之一（与英语 whether 同源）

definition_zh: 中子；原子核中不带电的粒子；中子星中的致密物质成分
definition_en: a nuclear particle with almost the same mass as a proton but no electric charge
core_image: 一颗与质子几乎同样重的小球从秤上走过，电荷表却始终指着零
scene: 反应堆的水池边，仪器记录到一个不带电的粒子撞进铀核。A slow neutron split the uranium nucleus and started a chain of reactions.
sceneCN: 这里 neutron 指「原子核中不带电的粒子」（第 1 个义项：质量与质子相近但不带电荷的核粒子）；句意：一个慢中子在铀核上引发裂变，并开启了一连串反应。图中可辨识物件：水池、铀棒、探测器、计数屏。

derivatives.zh: 中子物质（假想的纯中子物质）

senses.title: The charge-free nucleon
senses.definition: the nuclear particle that has nearly the mass of a proton but carries no electric charge
senses.definitionCN: 质量接近质子、但不带电荷的核粒子
senses.example: A helium nucleus contains two protons and two neutrons.
senses.exampleCN: 一个氦核含两个质子与两个中子。
senses.why: Latin neuter means 'neither of the two', and this particle is neither positive nor negative, so the name records its missing charge.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「两者皆非」正好描述这颗既不正也不负的粒子，名字记下的就是它缺了电荷。

senses.title: The mass that names an isotope
senses.titleCN: 决定同位素编号的那部分质量
senses.definition: the count of neutrons that, added to the proton count, gives the mass number of an isotope
senses.definitionCN: 中子数目与质子数目相加，得出某种同位素的质量数
senses.example: Carbon-14 carries two more neutrons than the common form of carbon.
senses.exampleCN: 碳十四比常见的碳多两个中子。
senses.why: Protons fix the element while neutrons vary, so the neutron count is what separates one isotope from another.
senses.whyCN: 质子固定元素，中子却可变，因此中子数正是区分同位素的那一项。

senses.title: A free neutron that falls apart
senses.definition: a neutron outside a nucleus, which decays within minutes into a proton, an electron and an antineutrino
senses.definitionCN: 脱离原子核的中子，会在几分钟内衰变成一个质子、一个电子与一个反中微子
senses.example: A free neutron lasts only about a quarter of an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 自由中子只存在大约一刻钟。
senses.why: Outside the stabilizing grip of a nucleus the neutron is unstable, and this slow decay became a standard example of beta decay.
senses.whyCN: 离开原子核的稳定约束后中子会变得不稳定，这一缓慢衰变成了贝塔衰变的标准例子。

senses.title: The trigger of a chain reaction
senses.definition: a neutron that enters a heavy nucleus and causes it to split, releasing further neutrons
senses.definitionCN: 进入重核并使其裂开、同时放出更多中子的粒子
senses.example: One neutron can start a chain that releases enormous heat.
senses.exampleCN: 一个中子就能开启释放巨大热量的链式反应。
senses.why: Because it carries no charge, a neutron can approach a nucleus without being pushed away, which makes it the ideal trigger.
senses.whyCN: 不带电的中子不会被原子核排斥，因此成为最理想的引发者。

senses.title: The probe for hidden atoms
senses.definition: a neutron used in scattering or diffraction experiments to locate light atoms that X-rays barely see
senses.definitionCN: 在散射或衍射实验中用来定位轻原子的中子，而这类原子用射线很难看清
senses.example: Neutron scattering showed where the hydrogen atoms sat in the lattice.
senses.exampleCN: 中子散射显示出氢原子在晶格中的位置。
senses.why: Neutrons scatter off nuclei rather than electrons, so they reveal hydrogen, which is nearly invisible to other probes.
senses.whyCN: 中子与原子核而非电子发生散射，因此能显示几乎对其他探针隐形的氢。

senses.title: The matter of a neutron star
senses.definition: the densely packed neutron matter left behind when a massive star collapses
senses.definitionCN: 大质量恒星坍缩后留下的致密中子物质
senses.example: A teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh as much as a mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 一茶匙中子星物质就会重如一座山。
senses.why: Gravity crushes electrons and protons together into neutrons, so the star is described by the particle it is made of.
senses.whyCN: 引力把电子与质子压成中子，因此这颗星就用构成它的粒子来命名。

senses.title: The particle slowed on purpose
senses.definition: a neutron reduced in speed by a moderator so that it is more likely to split uranium
senses.definitionCN: 经慢化剂降低速度、从而更容易引发铀裂变的中子
senses.example: Water acts as a moderator because it slows neutrons without absorbing too many.
senses.exampleCN: 水充当慢化剂，因为它让中子减速，又不会吸收太多。
senses.why: Slow neutrons spend more time near a nucleus and are far more likely to be captured, so reactors deliberately slow them.
senses.whyCN: 慢中子在核旁停留更久，被俘获的机会大得多，因此反应堆有意让它减速。

senses.title: The burst of a neutron weapon
senses.titleCN: 中子武器释放的高速粒子流
senses.definition: a flux of fast neutrons produced by a small nuclear device designed to irradiate rather than flatten
senses.definitionCN: 由小型核装置产生的高速中子流，其设计目的是辐照而非摧毁建筑
senses.example: The neutron bomb was meant to leave buildings standing.
senses.exampleCN: 中子弹的设计意图是让建筑物保持不倒。
senses.why: Weapons that emphasize this particle rather than blast heat were named after it, since the prompt radiation does the damage.
senses.whyCN: 这种武器强调粒子而非爆炸热，由于造成伤害的是瞬时辐射，便以该粒子命名。

intro.en: Neutron joins Latin neuter 'neither' to the -on ending already used in proton and electron. The particle was named in the early 1930s. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语「两者皆非」接到已在质子、电子里使用的同一个词尾上；这个粒子在二十世纪三十年代初获得命名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Neuter is ne 'not' plus uter 'either of two', so it means 'neither the one nor the other'.
items.cn: neuter 由「不」加「两者之一」构成，意为「两者都不是」。

items.en: Grammarians already used neuter for the gender that is neither masculine nor feminine, a ready-made label for a charge that is neither positive nor negative.
items.cn: 语法学家早已用这个词指既非阳性也非阴性的中性，正好可以用来标出既不正也不负的电荷。

items.en: In the early 1930s the neutral particle found in nuclear reactions took the name neutron, following the pattern of proton and electron.
items.cn: 二十世纪三十年代初，核反应中发现的不带电粒子依照质子与电子的构词方式得名中子。

items.en: With the first chain reactions the word spread into engineering: slow neutron, moderator, neutron number all date from this period.
items.cn: 随着最初的链式反应，这个词进入工程领域：慢中子、慢化剂、中子数都出自这一时期。

items.en: The 1960s added neutron star to the language, extending the particle's name to a whole kind of collapsed star.
items.cn: 二十世纪六十年代又添了「中子星」，把这一粒子的名字扩展到一整类坍缩恒星。

items.en: Exact first citations for the technical compounds are approximate; the core word and its Latin base are well recorded.
items.cn: 各技术复合词的最早书证年代为约数；核心词及其拉丁语来源都有充分记录。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes that share the neutral idea or merely the ending; group two holds the nuclear particles it is balanced against.
note.cn: 第一组是共享「中性」概念或仅仅共享词尾的形近词；第二组是常与它对照的核粒子。

entries.definition: Coined in Italian as a diminutive of neutro 'neutral': a tiny neutral particle with almost no mass, named by analogy, not by descent from neutron.
entries.definitionCN: 在意大利语里由「中性的」加指小成分造出：一种几乎没有质量的中性小粒子，是类比命名，并非从中子派生。

entries.definition: The Latin adjective itself, used in English for the neither gender or for a neutered animal; it is the direct source of the particle's first element.
entries.definitionCN: 就是那个拉丁形容词，英语里指中性性别或已绝育的动物；它是这个粒子词首成分的直接来源。

entries.definition: From the same ne plus uter stock: neither side in a dispute, or no net charge in physics.
entries.definitionCN: 出自同一「不」加「两者之一」的词源：争执中不站任何一方，物理上指没有净电荷。

entries.definition: From Greek neuron 'sinew, nerve': a nerve cell, sharing the ending only and nothing of the root.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊语「筋、神经」：指神经细胞，只共享词尾，与词根无关。

entries.definition: The positively charged nucleon of the same mass; together they form the nucleus and are called nucleons.
entries.definitionCN: 质量相同而带正电的核子；两者共同构成原子核，合称核子。

entries.definition: The covering name for a proton or a neutron, used when the distinction between them does not matter.
entries.definitionCN: 质子或中子的统称，在不需要区分两者时使用。

entries.definition: The very light negative particle of the atom; unlike the neutron it is not a nucleon and does not sit in the nucleus.
entries.definitionCN: 原子中极轻的负电粒子；与中子不同，它不是核子，也不住在核内。

entries.definition: A short-lived particle made of a quark and an antiquark; the ending is shared, the constitution is entirely different.
entries.definitionCN: 由一个夸克与一个反夸克组成的短命粒子；词尾相同，构成却完全不同。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin neuter 'neither' plus the -on ending: the particle that is neither positive nor negative.
normal.cn: 拉丁语「两者皆非」加同一个粒子词尾：既不正也不负的粒子。

normal.en: The family runs neutron, neutronic, antineutron, neutronium, neutron-rich.
normal.cn: 同族词包括中子、中子的、反中子、中子物质、富中子的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its roles: neutron star, neutron scattering, neutron moderator.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用途：中子星、中子散射、中子慢化剂。

normal.en: Isotopes are told apart by their neutron number, not by their proton number.
normal.cn: 区分同位素靠中子数，而不是质子数。

normal.en: The same neutral root appears in neuter, neutral and neutrino, though the last is an Italian coinage.
normal.cn: 同一个「中性」词根出现在中性、中立的词与中微子里，不过最后一个是在意大利语里造的。

abstract.en: Picture a guest of the same weight as the host who pays no entrance fee of charge.
abstract.cn: 想象一位与主人同样重、却不用交电荷门票的客人。

abstract.en: Picture a key with no metal that still opens the heavy door because nothing pushes it back.
abstract.cn: 想象一把没有金属的钥匙，因为不会被推回，照样打开重门。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that reads the same weight twice but shows zero on the charge dial.
abstract.cn: 想象一台秤两次读出同样的重量，电荷表盘却始终是零。

examples.en: Ordinary hydrogen has a nucleus of one proton and no neutron.
examples.cn: 普通氢的原子核只有一个质子，没有中子。

examples.en: Boron absorbs a neutron and becomes a different isotope.
examples.cn: 硼吸收一个中子后变成另一种同位素。

examples.en: Neutron stars are the leftover cores of exploded massive stars.
examples.cn: 中子星是爆发后的大质量恒星留下的核心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「neutral（中性）」的核里那颗球——既不吸也不斥，就是中子

root: 拉丁 neuter「两者皆非」= ne「不」+ uter「两者之一」；加 -on 粒子结尾。英语 neutron。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one chargeless particle: first the nuclear member and the isotope count, then its solitary decay, its work as a trigger, a probe, a star's material, a deliberately slowed tool and finally a weapon's burst.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一颗不带电的粒子走：先是核内成员与同位素计数，再是它的孤独衰变、作为引发者、作为探针、作为恒星材料、被人为减速的工具，最后是武器释放的粒子流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ball of the same weight as its neighbour that never registers on the charge dial.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗与邻居同样重、却从不在电荷表上留下读数的小球。

branches.en: THE BALLAST: inside the nucleus the neutron adds weight and no charge, and its number separates isotopes.
branches.cn: 压舱物：在核内它只添重量不添电荷，其数目把同位素分开。

branches.en: THE LONER: once outside the nucleus it cannot hold itself together and falls into a proton and an electron.
branches.cn: 孤独者：一旦离开原子核，它维持不住自己，裂成一个质子与一个电子。

branches.en: THE KEY: no charge means no repulsion, so the neutron can enter a nucleus and split it, especially when slowed.
branches.cn: 钥匙：不带电就不被排斥，因此能进入核内使之裂开，减速之后尤其容易。

branches.en: THE LANTERN: scattering off nuclei lets it show where hydrogen hides.
branches.cn: 灯：与原子核散射，使它照出氢藏在何处。

branches.en: THE EXTREME: crushed into a star it becomes the matter itself, and released in a burst it becomes a weapon's edge.
branches.cn: 极端：被压进恒星时它成为物质本身，被成束放出时又成为武器的锋刃。

intro.en: Neutron is a Latin-based coinage: a Latin adjective of neutrality plus the scientific ending shared with proton and electron.
intro.cn: 中子是以拉丁语为基础的造词：一个表示中性的拉丁形容词，加上与质子、电子共享的科学词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin neuter and its root uter also yield neuter, neutral and neutrality in English; the particle ending -on was added by physicists.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的中性形式及其词根还衍生出英语里的中性、中立的与中立状态；粒子结尾则由物理学家加上。

items.example: The negative particle turns an either-or word into a neither word.
items.exampleCN: 这个否定小品词把「二者之一」变成「二者皆非」。

items.structure: uter, utra, utrum (Latin adjective, 'either of two')
items.example: The adjective asks which of two things is meant.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词用来问两者之中指哪一个。

items.meaning: neither the one nor the other
items.example: The neuter form belongs to neither of the other two.
items.exampleCN: 中性形式不属于另外两者中的任何一个。

items.meaning: taking no side; having no net charge
items.meaningCN: 不站边的；没有净电荷的
items.example: A neutral atom balances its charges.
items.exampleCN: 中性原子使电荷保持平衡。

items.example: The neutron carries no charge at all.
items.exampleCN: 中子完全不带电荷。

items.example: Neutronic analysis predicts the reactor's behaviour.
items.exampleCN: 中子学分析可预测反应堆的行为。

items.example: The neutrino passes through matter almost untouched.
items.exampleCN: 中微子几乎不受阻碍地穿过物质。

items.example: An antineutron annihilates on contact with a neutron.
items.exampleCN: 反中子一碰到中子便湮灭。

latinEntries.meaning: which of the two; either of the two

definition_zh: 然而；尽管如此；不过
definition_en: in spite of that; however; used to introduce a statement that stands despite what came before
core_image: 门上挂着“禁止进入”的牌子，人还是推门走了进去
scene: 小路封了，一半还泡着水，徒步者却还是跨过告示牌继续走。The trail is closed and half flooded; nevertheless, a hiker steps past the sign and walks on.
sceneCN: 这里 nevertheless 是「尽管如此、仍然」（第 1 个义项：让步之后仍然成立）；句意：步道已经封闭、有一半被水淹，尽管如此，一名徒步者还是绕过告示牌继续往前走。图中可辨识物件：封闭告示牌、积水步道、徒步者的登山杖、黄黑警示带；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 然而；尽管如此；不过（连接性副词，承接前文并转折）

collocations.zh: 尽管如此，事实仍然不变

derivatives.zh: 尽管如此（同构的并列复合词，用 none 代替 never）
从不；决不（构词成分，此处原义为“一点也不”）
曾经；无论何时（never 的第二成分）
更少的；更少地（构词成分，比较级）
除非（同出 less 的复合连词）
减少；减轻（less 加 -en 构成的动词）

senses.title: In spite of that: opening a sentence against expectation
senses.titleCN: 尽管如此：开门见山地逆着预期说
senses.definition: used at the start of a sentence to say that what follows is true in spite of what was just said
senses.definitionCN: 用于句首，表示接下来的内容尽管有前文所说的情况仍然成立
senses.example: The hotel was full. Nevertheless, we found a room nearby.
senses.exampleCN: 旅馆客满了。尽管如此，我们还是在附近找到了一间房。
senses.why: Nevertheless is never plus the less, literally 'not any the less'. What came before does not make the next statement any smaller, so the sentence opens by refusing to be reduced.
senses.whyCN: nevertheless 是 never 加 the less，字面是“一点也不因此减少”。前文并没有让后一句变小，所以这个句子一开口就拒绝被削减。

senses.title: Joining two clauses after a semicolon
senses.definition: used after a semicolon to link two clauses and mark the second as a contrast
senses.definitionCN: 用于分号之后连接两个小句，并标记后一句为转折
senses.example: The evidence was thin; nevertheless, the jury convicted.
senses.exampleCN: 证据薄弱；尽管如此，陪审团仍判定有罪。
senses.why: As a conjunctive adverb it carries the contrast across the punctuation. The 'not any the less' still measures the second clause against the first.
senses.whyCN: 作为连接性副词，它把转折跨过标点带过去。“一点也不因此减少”仍在用前一句来衡量后一句。

senses.title: After but: the doubled contrast
senses.titleCN: 跟在 but 之后：双重的转折
senses.definition: used with but to add emphasis, as in 'cheap but nevertheless good'
senses.definitionCN: 与 but 连用以加强转折，如 cheap but nevertheless good
senses.example: The plan was expensive but nevertheless worth every penny.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划很贵，但尽管如此，每一分钱都值得。
senses.why: But already turns the sentence; nevertheless adds that the earlier fact does not reduce the later one. The two markers reinforce rather than contradict each other.
senses.whyCN: but 已经让句子转向；nevertheless 再补上一层：前面的事实并不能削减后面的事实。两个标记是相互加强，而不是相互矛盾。

senses.title: At the end: a trailing afterthought
senses.titleCN: 放在句尾：事后的补一句
senses.definition: placed at the end of a clause to add a delayed contrast, often after a pause
senses.definitionCN: 放在小句末尾，补充一个迟来的转折，常出现在停顿之后
senses.example: It was a foolish plan. He went ahead, nevertheless.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个愚蠢的计划。他还是照做了，尽管如此。
senses.why: The word can trail because the comparison is still live: the action is measured against the warning and is 'none the less' for it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以拖在句尾，因为比较仍然有效：行动相对于警告被衡量，而它“并未因此减少”。

senses.title: Academic concession: grant the objection, keep the claim
senses.titleCN: 学术让步：承认异议，保留论点
senses.definition: used in argument to admit a limitation and still maintain the main claim
senses.definitionCN: 用于论证中，承认某项局限，同时仍然坚持主要论点
senses.example: The sample is small; nevertheless, the result is suggestive.
senses.exampleCN: 样本很小；尽管如此，这一结果仍有提示意义。
senses.why: The concession lowers the claim's strength, and nevertheless says the claim is not lowered by that amount. It is the written form of 'none the less'.
senses.whyCN: 让步降低了论点的强度，而 nevertheless 说论点并没有因此降低那么多。它就是书面语里的“none the less”。

senses.title: Personal admission: I knew, and did it anyway
senses.titleCN: 个人承认：我知道，可我还是做了
senses.definition: used to admit a fault or risk and still report the action taken
senses.definitionCN: 用于承认过错或风险，却仍然陈述已经采取的行动
senses.example: I knew the risk; nevertheless, I signed.
senses.exampleCN: 我知道有风险；尽管如此，我还是签了。
senses.why: Here the first clause is self-criticism. Nevertheless refuses to let the admission cancel the act, so the person owns both at once.
senses.whyCN: 这里前一句是自我批评。nevertheless 不让这份承认取消行动，于是这个人同时承认了两件事。

senses.title: Formal register: the steady voice of statutes
senses.titleCN: 正式语体：法条里沉稳的声音
senses.definition: used in legal, official, and technical prose as a formal alternative to 'but' or 'however'
senses.definitionCN: 在法律、公文与技术写作中作为 but 或 however 的正式替代
senses.example: The notice was defective; nevertheless, it had legal effect.
senses.exampleCN: 该通知存在瑕疵；尽管如此，它仍具有法律效力。
senses.why: The compound is long and steady, and its 'none the less' logic suits rules that survive exceptions. Formal prose prefers it to a bare but.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词长而稳，其“并未减少”的逻辑正合那些在例外之后仍然存活的规则。正式写作偏爱它，而不是光秃秃的 but。

senses.title: Narrative: obstacles listed, outcome unchanged
senses.titleCN: 叙事：障碍列举完，结果不变
senses.definition: used in storytelling after a list of difficulties to show the result still happened
senses.definitionCN: 在叙事中用于列举困难之后，表示结果仍然发生
senses.example: Rain, delays and lost luggage — nevertheless, they arrived on time.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨、延误、行李丢失——尽管如此，他们还是准时到了。
senses.why: Each obstacle would normally count against the outcome. The word gathers them and says the outcome is none the less for all of them.
senses.whyCN: 每一项障碍通常都会对结果不利。这个词把它们收拢起来，说结果并没有因为这一切而减少。

senses.title: Emphatic: after an extreme list, the result still stands
senses.titleCN: 强调：极端情况之后，结果仍然成立
senses.definition: used after the strongest possible objection to insist that the result stands
senses.definitionCN: 用于最强的反对意见之后，坚持结果仍然成立
senses.example: Every forecast said failure; nevertheless, the launch succeeded.
senses.exampleCN: 所有预测都说会失败；尽管如此，发射还是成功了。
senses.why: The stronger the objection, the more the 'not any the less' has to do. Here the word is close to 'against all of it'.
senses.whyCN: 反对越强，“一点也不因此减少”要做的功就越大。这里的词义接近“对抗这一切”。

senses.title: The fixed frame: it is nevertheless true that
senses.titleCN: 固定框架：it is nevertheless true that
senses.definition: used in the frame 'it is nevertheless true that' to affirm a fact after doubt has been raised
senses.definitionCN: 用于 it is nevertheless true that 这一框架，在被质疑之后仍然肯定某一事实
senses.example: It is nevertheless true that the method saved lives.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管如此，这个方法确实救过人命，这一点是真的。
senses.why: The frame places truth itself on the far side of the contrast: whatever was argued, the fact is none the less true.
senses.whyCN: 这个框架把“真”本身放到转折的另一边：无论前面争论了什么，事实并未因此而不真。

intro.en: Nevertheless began as the phrase never the less, written neuer þe lesse in the early 14c. and joined into one word by the mid-14c. Its never does not mean 'never' but 'not at all, none the', as in never the wiser.
intro.cn: nevertheless 起初是短语 never the less，14 世纪早期写作 neuer þe lesse，到 14 世纪中期合成一词。其中的 never 不是“永不”，而是“一点也不、none the”，如 never the wiser。

items.en: First recorded in the early 14c. as the phrase neuer þe lesse, still written in separate parts.
items.cn: 最早记录于 14 世纪早期，写作短语 neuer þe lesse，各部分仍分开书写。

items.en: By the mid-14c. the parts are joined as neuerþeles, and the word begins to work as a single adverb.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪中期，各部分合成 neuerþeles，这个词开始作为单一副词使用。

items.en: Middle English also had neverthelater, never-less, ner-the-less, never-later and not-the-less, all built on the same 'none the less' pattern.
items.cn: 中古英语还有 neverthelater、never-less、ner-the-less、never-later、not-the-less 等变体，都建立在同一个“none the less”模式上。

items.en: Never comes from Old English næfre, itself ne 'not' plus æfre 'ever'.
items.cn: never 来自古英语 næfre，本身由 ne“不”加 æfre“曾经”构成。

items.en: Modern English keeps nevertheless beside nonetheless; the two are parallel compounds, one with never and one with none.
items.cn: 现代英语让 nevertheless 与 nonetheless 并存；两者是并列复合词，一个用 never，一个用 none。

note.en: The first group shares the never-the-less shape or its parts, the second shares the contrastive meaning.
note.cn: 第一组共享 never-the-less 的结构或其组成部分，第二组共享转折的词义。

entries.definition: in spite of that. It is built exactly like nevertheless but with none instead of never, and the two are interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管如此。它的构造与 nevertheless 完全相同，只是用 none 代替 never，两者可以互换。

entries.definition: the older phrase written in separate words. It shows the literal parts: never, the, less.
entries.definitionCN: 分开书写的较早短语。它显示了这个词的字面成分：never、the、less。

entries.definition: an obsolete variant of nevertheless, built with later instead of less. It shows how freely the pattern was varied.
entries.definitionCN: nevertheless 的废弃变体，用 later 而不是 less。它说明这个模式当年被替换得多么自由。

entries.definition: in whatever way, or used to introduce a contrast. It is the general-purpose connector, while nevertheless is heavier and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 无论如何；然而。它是通用连接词，而 nevertheless 更重、更正式。

entries.definition: in spite of; despite. It often works as a preposition or a formal connector, and is even heavier than nevertheless.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管；虽然。它常作介词或正式连接词，比 nevertheless 还要重。

entries.definition: in spite of that, used in speech. It carries the same turn but sounds conversational rather than written.
entries.definitionCN: 即使如此。它带有同样的转折，但听起来是口语而非书面语。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: never here means 'not at all', less is a comparative, and the Middle English variants all repeat the same pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：这里的 never 意为“一点也不”，less 是比较级，而中古英语的各种变体都重复同一个模式。

normal.en: Never in this word is not 'never': it means 'not at all, none the', as in never the wiser or never the worse.
normal.cn: 这个词里的 never 不是“永不”：它意为“一点也不、none the”，如 never the wiser、never the worse。

normal.en: the less is a comparative. Together the parts say 'not any the less', which is why the later clause is not reduced.
normal.cn: the less 是比较级。合起来说“一点也不因此减少”，这正是后一句没有被削减的原因。

normal.en: Middle English had neverthelater, never-less, ner-the-less and not-the-less, all variations on the same comparison.
normal.cn: 中古英语有 neverthelater、never-less、ner-the-less、not-the-less，都是同一个比较结构的变体。

normal.en: Nonetheless is the twin: same building plan, with none instead of never.
normal.cn: nonetheless 是它的双胞胎：同样的建筑图纸，只用 none 代替 never。

normal.en: But nevertheless is a standard frame: but turns the sentence, nevertheless insists nothing was lost in the turn.
normal.cn: but nevertheless 是标准框架：but 让句子转向，nevertheless 坚持这次转向没有损失任何东西。

abstract.en: A door marked NO ENTRY, already pushed half open: the warning is real, and the step is still taken.
abstract.cn: 一扇写着“禁止入内”的门已被推开一半：警告是真的，脚步还是迈了出去。

abstract.en: A line that bends at an obstacle and then continues in the same direction: the bend does not shorten the road.
abstract.cn: 一条线在障碍处弯了一下，然后继续朝同一方向走：弯折并没有让路变短。

abstract.en: A hand pressing down on a box while another hand still lifts it: the weight is counted, and the lift still happens.
abstract.cn: 一只手向下压箱子，另一只手仍把它抬起：重量被算进去了，抬起仍然发生。

examples.en: The instructions were unclear; nevertheless, the team finished on time.
examples.cn: 说明不清楚；尽管如此，团队还是按时完成了。

examples.en: He was warned about the ice, but nevertheless he walked out onto the lake.
examples.cn: 有人警告过他冰面危险，但尽管如此，他还是走上了湖面。

examples.en: It is nevertheless true that the old bridge has carried the town's traffic for a century.
examples.cn: 尽管如此，这座老桥确实已经承载了小镇一个世纪的交通，这一点是真的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「那我也赖着」——尽管被赶、被劝，那我也赖着不走 → nevertheless 尽管如此、仍然

root: 由 never“一点也不、none the”＋ the ＋ less（比较级）构成的复合副词，14 世纪早期写作 neuer þe lesse；never 来自古英语 næfre＝ ne“不”＋ æfre“曾经”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of nevertheless all carry one comparison: whatever was said, the next statement is 'none the less'. The word changes position and register, from sentence opening to trailing afterthought, from academic concession to legal prose.
sensesIntro.cn: nevertheless 的十个义项都带着同一个比较：无论前面说了什么，后一句都“并未因此减少”。这个词改变的是位置与语体，从句首到句尾补语，从学术让步到法律文书。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed sign on a door that is opened anyway.
core.cn: 核心意象：门上的封闭告示，而门还是被推开了。

branches.en: SENTENCE POSITIONS: opening a new sentence, and joining two clauses after a semicolon.
branches.cn: 句子位置：开启一个新句子，以及在分号后连接两个小句。

branches.en: DOUBLED AND TRAILING: after but for extra emphasis, and at the end as a delayed afterthought.
branches.cn: 加倍与拖尾：跟在 but 后加强语气，以及放在句尾作迟来的补语。

branches.en: PERSONAL AND ARGUMENTATIVE CONCESSION: granting a limitation, and admitting a fault while acting anyway.
branches.cn: 论证与个人的让步：承认局限，以及承认过错却仍然行动。

branches.en: REGISTER AND NARRATIVE: the steady voice of statutes, and obstacles listed before an unchanged outcome.
branches.cn: 语体与叙事：法条沉稳的声音，以及列举障碍后结果依旧。

branches.en: MAXIMUM RESISTANCE: after the strongest objection, and in the fixed frame it is nevertheless true that.
branches.cn: 最大阻力：最强反对之后，以及 it is nevertheless true that 这一固定框架。

intro.en: Nevertheless is a compound, not a suffixed word: never plus the plus less. English keeps the same plan in nonetheless, and the parts survive separately in never, ever, less, unless and lessen.
intro.cn: nevertheless 是复合词，不是加后缀的词：never 加 the 加 less。英语用同一图纸造出 nonetheless，而各成分分别活在 never、ever、less、unless、lessen 中。

latinIntro.en: Nevertheless is Germanic. The Latin entries below are counterparts for contrast: nihilominus and tamen both mean 'nevertheless', and minus supplies 'less'.
latinIntro.cn: nevertheless 属日耳曼语。下面的拉丁词是对照用的对应词：nihilominus 与 tamen 都表示“尽管如此”，minus 提供“更少”。

items.meaning: in spite of that; none the less
items.meaningCN: 尽管如此；并未因此减少（never“一点也不”+ the + less 比较级）
items.example: The road was closed; nevertheless, we reached the village.
items.exampleCN: 道路封闭了；尽管如此，我们还是到了村子。

items.meaningCN: 尽管如此（none“一点也不”+ the + less，与 nevertheless 同构）
items.example: The sample was small; nonetheless, the pattern was clear.
items.exampleCN: 样本虽小；尽管如此，规律仍然清楚。

items.example: He never spoke of the accident again.
items.exampleCN: 他再也没有提起那次事故。

items.meaningCN: 曾经；无论何时（never 的第二成分）
items.example: Have you ever seen the tide come in this fast?
items.exampleCN: 你见过潮水涨得这么快的景象吗？

items.meaning: a smaller amount; not as much
items.meaningCN: 更少的；更少地（little 的比较级）
items.example: This route takes less time than the motorway.
items.exampleCN: 这条路线比高速公路花的时间更少。

items.meaningCN: 除非（由 on lesse“在少于……的条件下”演变而来）
items.example: We will go unless it rains.
items.exampleCN: 除非下雨，否则我们就去。

items.meaningCN: 减少；减轻（less + -en 构成动词）
items.example: The medicine lessened the pain within an hour.
items.exampleCN: 药物在一小时内减轻了疼痛。

items.meaningCN: 较小的；次要的（less 再加 -er 的历史双重比较级）
items.example: The lesser of the two risks was still serious.
items.exampleCN: 两个风险中较小的那个仍然很严重。

items.example: The raven said, 'Nevermore.'
items.exampleCN: 那只渡鸦说：“再也不了。”

items.meaningCN: 永无止境的（never + ending，复合形容词）
items.example: The repairs felt like a never-ending task.
items.exampleCN: 这些修缮活像一项永无止境的任务。

definition_zh: 报纸；一份报纸；报社
definition_en: a printed publication, usually issued daily or weekly, containing news, articles and advertisements
core_image: 折叠的报纸摊在餐桌上，一角被咖啡杯压住，露出半截头条
scene: 早餐桌上一杯咖啡压着摊开的报纸，父亲边喝边翻到体育版。He reads a newspaper every morning before work.
sceneCN: 这里 newspaper 是「报纸」（第 1 个义项：刊载新闻的印刷出版物）；句意为他每天上班前都读一份报纸。图中可辨识物件：咖啡杯、摊开的报纸、餐桌。

derivatives.zh: 由 news 与 print 复合，义为「新闻纸」
由 newspaper 与 man 复合，义为「报人；男记者」
由 newspaper 与 woman 复合，义为「女报人；女记者」

senses.title: A printed publication with news
senses.definition: a set of printed sheets, usually published daily or weekly, containing news, articles and advertisements
senses.definitionCN: 通常每日或每周出版、刊载新闻、文章与广告的一套印刷纸张
senses.example: The newspaper printed the story on its front page.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报纸把这条新闻登在了头版。
senses.why: The compound joins news with paper, so the name literally points to the sheets that carry the reports.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把 news 与 paper 拼在一起，字面上就指向承载报道的那些纸张。

senses.title: A single copy or issue
senses.definition: one copy or one day's issue of such a publication
senses.definitionCN: 这样一份出版物的一份或某一期
senses.example: She bought a newspaper from the stand on the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 她从街角的报刊亭买了一份报纸。
senses.why: Once the sheets become a product, the same word can count them one by one in a reader's hands.
senses.whyCN: 当这些纸张变成商品，同一个词就能在读者手里把它们一份一份地数出来。

senses.title: The organization that publishes it
senses.definition: the company or office that produces a newspaper
senses.definitionCN: 生产这份报纸的公司或办公机构
senses.example: He has worked for the same newspaper for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在同一家报社工作了二十年。
senses.why: A paper is also the people who write and print it, so the word slides from the object to the institution behind it.
senses.whyCN: 一份报纸也指写它、印它的那些人，于是词义从物件滑到它背后的机构。

intro.en: Newspaper joins the English word news to paper, a word that came from Latin through Old French and named the material before it named the publication.
intro.cn: newspaper 把英语的 news 与 paper 组合起来；paper 经古法语来自拉丁语，先指材料，后指出版物。

items.en: Papyrus was the writing reed of the ancient world and gave Latin its word for paper.
items.cn: papyrus 是古代用来书写的芦苇，也是拉丁语中「纸」一词的来源。

items.en: Old French shortened papyrus into papier, the material on which words were written.
items.cn: 古法语把 papyrus 缩成 papier，指书写文字所用的材料。

items.en: Middle English paper named the material and later a sheet or a document made from it.
items.cn: 中古英语 paper 指纸张材料，后来也指用纸做成的一页或一份文件。

items.en: News and paper were combined into newspaper for the printed sheets that carried reports.
items.cn: news 与 paper 组合成 newspaper，指承载报道的印刷纸张。

items.en: Modern English uses newspaper for the printed product, a single issue and the company that publishes it.
items.cn: 现代英语用 newspaper 指印刷品、单份报纸，也指出版它的公司。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on news or on the paper compound; the near-meaning group gathers other kinds of periodical publication.
note.cn: 形近组收以 news 或 paper 复合而成的词；近义组收其他类型的定期出版物。

entries.definition: Information about recent events; the first half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 关于近期事件的信息；这个复合词的前半部分。

entries.definition: The material made for writing and printing; the second half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 用于书写和印刷的材料；这个复合词的后半部分。

entries.definition: The cheap paper used for printing newspapers.
entries.definitionCN: 印刷报纸所用的廉价纸张。

entries.definition: A small stall where newspapers are sold.
entries.definitionCN: 出售报纸的小摊；报刊亭。

entries.definition: A periodical, often more serious or specialised than a newspaper.
entries.definitionCN: 定期刊物，常比报纸更严肃或更专业。

entries.definition: A small-format newspaper focused on sensation and pictures.
entries.definitionCN: 以小版面、耸动内容和图片为主的小报。

entries.definition: A large-format newspaper known for serious reporting.
entries.definitionCN: 以大版面、严肃报道著称的报纸。

entries.definition: Any publication that appears at regular intervals.
entries.definitionCN: 任何定期出版的刊物。

normalIntro.en: The word is a plain compound of news and paper, and its family keeps combining the report with the material or the place that sells it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 news 与 paper 的直接复合，词族不断把「报道」与材料或售卖地点结合起来。

normal.en: news plus paper equals the paper that carries the news.
normal.cn: news 加 paper 等于承载新闻的那种纸。

normal.en: Paper goes back to Latin papyrus, the reed once used for writing.
normal.cn: paper 可追到拉丁语 papyrus，那是古时用来书写的芦苇。

normal.en: One newspaper, two newspapers: count the physical copies with a plural.
normal.cn: one newspaper、two newspapers：用复数来数一份份实物。

normal.en: The newspaper can also mean the company, and then it takes a singular verb.
normal.cn: the newspaper 也可指公司，这时它接单数动词。

normal.en: The usual partners are daily newspaper, local newspaper and newspaper article.
normal.cn: 常见搭配有 daily newspaper、local newspaper 与 newspaper article。

abstract.en: A newspaper is news that has been given a body of paper and a daily habit.
abstract.cn: 报纸就是给新闻配上一副纸做的身体，再养成每天阅读的习惯。

abstract.en: The same word covers the object, the single copy and the institution because a paper exists only while all three hold together.
abstract.cn: 同一个词兼指物件、单份与机构，因为只有三者抱在一起，一份报纸才成立。

abstract.en: Every folded page is a day's worth of the world pressed flat.
abstract.cn: 每一页折起的纸，都是一天世界被压平的形状。

examples.en: He reads a newspaper every morning before work.
examples.cn: 他每天上班前都读一份报纸。

examples.en: The local newspaper sent a reporter to the school fair.
examples.cn: 地方报纸派了一名记者去学校集市。

examples.en: She wrapped the old plates in newspaper before putting them in the box.

core.cn: 核心意象：早餐桌上折叠的报纸，一角被咖啡杯压住。

branches.cn: 摊在杯子旁边的头版

branches.cn: 手里的一份报纸与做出它的报馆

definition_zh: 噩梦；梦魇；可怕的处境；令人恐惧的经历
definition_en: a frightening dream, especially one that wakes the sleeper; a very unpleasant or frightening situation or experience
core_image: 深夜床边一团沉重的黑影压在胸口，人想喊却发不出声
scene: 凌晨时分，床边有一团说不清的黑影压下来，人想翻身却动不了，喉咙里发不出声音。The child woke with a scream after a nightmare about a falling staircase.
sceneCN: 这里是「噩梦」（第 1 个义项：睡眠中令人恐惧的梦）；句意为孩子梦到楼梯塌落，惊叫着醒来。图中可辨识物件：床边黑影、被角、半开的窗。

pos.zh: 噩梦；梦魇；可怕的处境；令人恐惧的经历

collocations.zh: 最可怕的设想；噩梦般的情形
后勤上的噩梦；极难处理的事

derivatives.zh: 由 nightmare 加 -ish（像……的）构成，义为「噩梦般的；可怕的」
由 nightmarish 加 -ly 构成，义为「噩梦般地；可怕地」
由 nightmarish 加 -ness 构成，义为「噩梦般的性质；可怕程度」

senses.title: A frightening dream that wakes the sleeper
senses.titleCN: 噩梦；惊醒人的可怕梦境
senses.definition: a frightening dream, usually so vivid that the sleeper wakes in fear
senses.definitionCN: 令人恐惧的梦，通常逼真到使睡着的人惊醒
senses.example: She woke from a nightmare about falling off a bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 她从一个梦见自己从桥上坠落的噩梦中醒来。
senses.why: Old English niht meant night and mare named the demon believed to sit on a sleeper's chest, so the word began as a name for the pressure felt in the dark rather than for the story told afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 niht 是「夜」，mare 指传说中压在睡者胸口的恶魔，所以这个词最初命名的是黑暗中感到的那股压迫，而不是醒来后讲述的情节。

senses.title: The old demon held to sit on a sleeper's chest
senses.titleCN: 梦魇；旧指夜中压身的恶魔
senses.definition: in older use, an evil spirit believed to suffocate people in their sleep, together with the choking sensation it caused
senses.definitionCN: 旧时指被认为在睡眠中使人窒息的恶灵，以及它带来的压迫窒息感
senses.example: In the old tale, a nightmare crouched on the traveller's chest until dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个古老的故事里，一只梦魇蹲在旅人胸口直到天亮。
senses.why: Mare was a demon, not a horse, and the choking weight of sleep paralysis was explained as its body; the modern bad-dream sense grew straight out of that picture.
senses.whyCN: mare 是恶魔而不是母马，睡眠瘫痪时那种被压住的窒息感被解释成它的身体；现代「噩梦」的意思正是从这幅画面长出来的。

senses.title: A situation that feels like a bad dream
senses.titleCN: 可怕的处境；噩梦般的经历
senses.definition: a very unpleasant, difficult or frightening situation or experience
senses.definitionCN: 非常不愉快、艰难或令人恐惧的局面或经历
senses.example: The airport closure turned our trip into a nightmare.
senses.exampleCN: 机场关闭让我们的行程变成了一场噩梦。
senses.why: Once the word names a night terror, calling a day or a journey a nightmare borrows the same helpless fear into waking life, which is why the figurative use needs no new word.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词先命名夜里的恐惧，说某个白天或某趟行程是 nightmare，就是把这股无能为力的恐惧借到清醒生活里，所以比喻义不需要另造新词。

intro.en: Nightmare is a native English compound of night and a word for a demon, and its bad-dream sense is later than the demon it once named.
intro.cn: nightmare 是英语本土的复合词，由「夜」和一个指恶魔的词合成；「噩梦」义比它最初命名的恶魔出现得更晚。

items.en: Niht was the ordinary word for night and supplied the first half of the compound.
items.cn: niht 是古英语里表示「夜」的常用词，构成这个词的前半。

items.en: Mare named an evil spirit or incubus believed to press on sleepers, and it is a different word from mare meaning a female horse.
items.cn: mare 指被认为压住睡者的恶灵或梦淫妖，它与表示母马的 mare 是两个不同的词。

items.en: The compound first named the choking visitation and the terror that came with it, still close to the demon rather than to the dream.
items.cn: 这个复合词最初指夜间压身的侵扰和随之而来的恐惧，仍贴近恶魔本身而不是梦。

items.en: Writers began using nightmare for any frightening dream, and the demon faded into the background of the word; the exact date of this shift is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为，十六至十七世纪的作者开始用 nightmare 指任何可怕的梦，恶魔渐渐退到这个词的背景里；这一转变的确切年代存疑。

items.en: Modern English keeps the dream sense and extends it to any miserable or frightening situation, as in a nightmare journey.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「噩梦」义，并把它扩展到任何糟糕或可怕的情形，如 a nightmare journey。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same night element or sharing the spelling mare; the near-meaning group collects words for bad dreams and the fear they leave behind.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 night 成分构成的词，以及与 mare 拼写相同的词；近义组收表示噩梦和它留下的恐惧的词。

entries.definition: Built from nightmare with -ish, meaning like a nightmare.
entries.definitionCN: 由 nightmare 加 -ish 构成，义为「噩梦般的」。

entries.definition: A female horse, a separate word that merely shares the spelling of the demon in nightmare; the two are unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 母马，只是与 nightmare 里的恶魔同形，两者来源无关。

entries.definition: The time when night begins, built with the same night element.
entries.definitionCN: 夜幕降临的时刻，用了同一个 night 成分。

entries.definition: The hours of darkness, another compound on night.
entries.definitionCN: 黑夜的那段时间，另一个用 night 构成的复合词。

entries.definition: A dream that frightens or disturbs the sleeper, the plain phrase for the dream sense.
entries.definitionCN: 使睡着的人恐惧或不安的梦，是「噩梦」义的普通说法。

entries.definition: Extreme fear, the feeling a nightmare leaves behind.
entries.definitionCN: 极度的恐惧，是噩梦留下的感觉。

entries.definition: A strong feeling of fear and shock, often caused by something seen or imagined.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的恐惧与震惊，常由所见或想象之物引起。

entries.definition: A male demon said to lie upon sleepers, the learned name for the old nightmare creature.
entries.definitionCN: 传说中压住睡者的男性恶魔，是旧时 nightmare 所指之物的书面名称。

normalIntro.en: The word joins the Old English word for night to a demon that was blamed for a weight on the chest, and its later senses keep that picture of helpless fear.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把古英语的「夜」与一个被归咎于胸口重压的恶魔连在一起，后来的义项都保留着那种无力恐惧的画面。

normal.en: Niht is the Old English word for night, so the first half of nightmare is simply the dark hours.
normal.cn: niht 是古英语的「夜」，所以 nightmare 的前半就是那段黑暗的时间。

normal.en: Mare in this word is a demon, not a female horse; the shared spelling is a coincidence of two unrelated words.
normal.cn: 这个词里的 mare 是恶魔，不是母马；拼写相同只是两个无关词偶然撞在一起。

normal.en: The demon was blamed for the choking weight felt during sleep paralysis, which is why the word first meant that oppression.
normal.cn: 睡眠瘫痪时感到的压身窒息被归咎于这个恶魔，所以这个词最初指的就是那股压迫。

normal.en: The dream sense came later, when the demon was forgotten and only the terror of the dream remained.
normal.cn: 「梦」这个意思来得更晚：恶魔被遗忘之后，只剩梦里的恐惧留在词里。

normal.en: The figurative sense grows straight out of the dream: a nightmare journey is a waking experience that feels equally out of control.
normal.cn: 比喻义直接从梦里长出来：a nightmare journey 就是一段同样失控的清醒经历。

abstract.en: A word invented to explain a weight on the chest ends up naming a broken schedule, because both feel like something sitting on you that you cannot push off.
abstract.cn: 一个原本用来解释胸口重压的词，最后用来命名被打乱的日程，因为两者都像有东西压在身上、推不开。

abstract.en: Nightmare keeps two unrelated words in one shell, the demon and the horse, and only the demon shaped the meaning.
abstract.cn: nightmare 把一个恶魔和一个母马两个无关的词装进同一个外壳，真正塑造词义的只有那个恶魔。

abstract.en: Every figurative nightmare is a claim that the daytime world has started behaving like a bad dream, with no exit until you wake.
abstract.cn: 每一个比喻意义上的 nightmare，都是在说白天的世界开始像噩梦一样运转，不醒来就找不到出口。

examples.en: She woke from a nightmare about falling off a bridge.
examples.cn: 她从一个梦见自己从桥上坠落的噩梦中醒来。

examples.en: The flooding turned the rescue into a nightmare for the whole team.
examples.cn: 洪水让整个救援队陷入噩梦般的困境。

examples.en: He still has nightmares about the accident.
examples.cn: 他仍会梦到那场事故。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奈特妹儿」——夜里有个黑影压在身上，想喊也喊不出声；nightmare 就是噩梦。

root: 古英语 niht（夜）加 mare（传说中压住睡者的恶灵，一般认为与表示母马的 mare 无关）；词义由「夜间压身的恐惧」扩展为噩梦与可怕处境。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a night terror caused by a weight on the chest; the senses then divide into the bad dream, the old demon, and the waking situation that feels the same.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是夜里胸口受压带来的恐惧；义项由此分出噩梦、旧时的恶魔，以及感觉相同的清醒处境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy dark shape at the bedside pressing on the chest while the sleeper cannot speak.
core.cn: 核心意象：床边一团沉重的黑影压住胸口，睡着的人说不出话。

branches.en: a child sitting up in the dark, calling for a parent
branches.cn: 孩子在黑暗里坐起来喊父母

branches.en: an old woodcut of a demon crouched on a sleeper's chest
branches.cn: 一幅旧木刻里蹲在睡者胸口的恶魔

branches.en: the same choking weight described first as a spirit, then as a dream
branches.cn: 同一种压身的窒息感，先说成恶灵，后说成梦

branches.en: a cancelled flight turning a holiday into a nightmare
branches.cn: 航班取消，把假期变成噩梦

branches.en: a schedule so tight that every delay spreads
branches.cn: 紧到任何延误都会扩散的日程

intro.en: The word is held together by the Old English noun for night, the demon word mare, the compound they formed and the English endings that build its adjective and adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的「夜」、指恶魔的 mare、二者合成的复合词，以及构成形容词和副词的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.cn: nightmare 里的 mare 是日耳曼民间传说中的恶魔，没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此不列拉丁词条。
