definition_zh: 氮；氮气
definition_en: the chemical element of atomic number 7, a colourless, odourless gas that makes up about four fifths of the air
core_image: 一只无色气球悬在空气中，旁边一株豆科植物的根瘤被剖开露出粉红色内部
scene: 农夫轮种豆科作物，让土壤里的氮多起来，不必再买化肥。The farmer rotated legumes to add nitrogen to the soil without buying fertilizer.
sceneCN: 这里 nitrogen 指「土壤中的氮素养分」（第 3 个义项：氮肥与固氮）；豆科植物的根瘤菌把空气中的氮固定进土壤，农户因此不必买化肥。图中可辨识物件：豆科植株、根瘤剖面、土壤层、轮作示意牌；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 氮；氮气（不可数；化学式 N₂）

senses.title: The element
senses.definition: the chemical element with atomic number 7, a non-metal that forms strong triple bonds in its diatomic form
senses.definitionCN: 原子序数为 7 的元素，非金属，其双原子形式含牢固的三键
senses.example: Nitrogen has seven protons and typically seven neutrons.
senses.exampleCN: 氮有七个质子，通常也有七个中子。
senses.why: The name labels an element, not just the air gas, so it also applies to nitrogen atoms inside proteins and fertilisers.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字标的是元素而非仅仅是空气里的气体，因此蛋白质与肥料中的氮原子同样适用。

senses.title: The bulk gas of the air
senses.titleCN: 大气主体：约占空气五分之四的惰性气体
senses.definition: molecular N2, the inert gas that dilutes oxygen and fills most of the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 双原子分子 N₂，稀释氧、占据大气绝大部分的惰性气体
senses.example: Crisp packets are filled with nitrogen to stop the contents going stale.
senses.exampleCN: 薯片包装充入氮气，防止内容物变陈。
senses.why: Because the triple bond makes N2 unreactive, industry values it precisely for doing nothing.
senses.whyCN: 由于三键使 N₂ 极不活泼，工业看重的恰恰是它「什么都不做」。

senses.title: Soil fertility and fixation
senses.titleCN: 土壤氮素：固氮、施肥与轮作
senses.definition: the nitrogen available to plants in soil, supplied by fertiliser or by bacteria that fix atmospheric gas
senses.definitionCN: 土壤中可供植物利用的氮，来自肥料或固氮细菌
senses.example: Legumes add nitrogen to the soil through their root nodules.
senses.exampleCN: 豆科植物通过根瘤给土壤补充氮。
senses.why: Plants cannot use N2 directly, so agricultural usage names the usable forms, not the gas overhead.
senses.whyCN: 植物无法直接利用 N₂，因此农业用法指的是可利用的形态，而不是头顶上的气体。

senses.title: Inside proteins
senses.titleCN: 蛋白质中的氮：氨基酸的基本成分
senses.definition: the nitrogen bound in amino acids, and therefore in every protein and in DNA
senses.definitionCN: 结合在氨基酸中、从而存在于每种蛋白质与 DNA 中的氮
senses.example: Every amino acid carries at least one nitrogen atom.
senses.exampleCN: 每种氨基酸都至少带有一个氮原子。
senses.why: Life's chemistry is built on nitrogen-containing groups, so the element doubles as a marker of protein content.
senses.whyCN: 生命的化学建立在含氮基团之上，因此这个元素也成了蛋白质含量的标记。

senses.title: Liquid nitrogen
senses.titleCN: 液氮：极低温的冷却与保存介质
senses.definition: nitrogen cooled to about minus 196 degrees Celsius, used for freezing, storage and cooling
senses.definitionCN: 冷却到约零下 196 摄氏度的氮，用于冷冻、保存与降温
senses.example: Samples are stored in liquid nitrogen at the tissue bank.
senses.exampleCN: 组织库中的样本保存在液氮里。
senses.why: The boiling point of the gas is so low that its liquid becomes a standard laboratory coolant.
senses.whyCN: 这种气体的沸点极低，其液态因此成了实验室的标准冷却剂。

senses.title: Nitrogen oxides and smog
senses.titleCN: 氮氧化物：交通排放与光化学烟雾
senses.definition: the family of nitrogen-oxygen compounds, especially NO and NO2, formed in hot engines and driving photochemical smog
senses.definitionCN: 氮与氧的化合物一族，尤其是高温引擎生成的 NO 与 NO₂，会促成光化学烟雾
senses.example: Nitrogen oxides from traffic feed the smog over the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 交通排放的氮氧化物助长了谷地上空的光化学烟雾。
senses.why: Pollution control needed a short collective label, so the element name stands in for its troublesome compounds.
senses.whyCN: 污染控制需要一个简短的统称，于是元素名被用来指代它那些麻烦的化合物。

senses.title: The nitrogen cycle
senses.titleCN: 氮循环：在空气、土壤与生物之间流转
senses.definition: the circulation of nitrogen among the atmosphere, soil, water and living things through fixation, assimilation and denitrification
senses.definitionCN: 氮经固氮、同化与反硝化在大气、土壤、水体与生物之间循环
senses.example: The nitrogen cycle moves the element between air, soil and living things.
senses.exampleCN: 氮循环让这个元素在空气、土壤与生物之间流转。
senses.why: Because the element changes chemical form at every step, the cycle is named after the element rather than any one compound.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个元素在每一步都改变化学形态，循环便以元素而非某一种化合物命名。

senses.title: The nitre-former in the name
senses.definition: the sense recorded by the name itself: Chaptal named the gas because it was found in nitre, that is, saltpetre
senses.definitionCN: 名字本身记录的义项：夏普塔尔因这种气体存在于硝石（硝酸钾）中而为它命名
senses.example: The name nitrogen still says 'nitre-former', though the gas itself is inert.
senses.exampleCN: nitrogen 这个名字至今仍表示「硝石产生者」，尽管这种气体本身是惰性的。
senses.why: The French coinage nitrogene described where the element came from chemically, and English simply transliterated the claim.
senses.whyCN: 法语造词 nitrogene 描述的是该元素在化学上的来源，英语只是把这个说法音译过来。

intro.en: Nitrogen is a French scientific coinage of 1790, built from Greek nitron 'soda, nitre' and -genes 'producer'. Its first element was already ambiguous in ancient Greek.
intro.cn: nitrogen 是 1790 年的法语科学造词，由希腊 nitron「碱、硝石」与 -genes「产生者」构成。它的第一块在古代希腊语中就已含混。

items.en: Greek nitron named native soda, a mineral salt used in cleaning, not saltpetre. Latin nitrum later shifted the word toward saltpetre, and chemistry inherited the confusion.
items.cn: 希腊 nitron 指天然碱，一种用于洗涤的矿物盐，而非硝石。拉丁 nitrum 后来把这个词引向硝石，化学继承了这一混淆。

items.en: The suffix -genes 'born of, producing' comes from the root gen- 'to be born'. It marks the element as something that generates a named substance.
items.cn: 后缀 -genes「由……所生、产生」出自词根 gen-「出生」。它把这个元素标记为能生成某种特定物质的东西。

items.en: In 1790 the French chemist Chaptal coined nitrogene, because the gas was obtained from nitre and seemed to be the nitre-forming principle. The claim was later revised.
items.cn: 1790 年法国化学家夏普塔尔造出 nitrogene，因为这种气体可从硝石取得，似乎是成硝石的本原。这一说法后来被修正。

items.en: English nitrogen appears in the 1790s, transliterating the French term as the new chemistry spread. Before that the gas was called 'dephlogisticated air' or 'mephitic air'.
items.cn: 英语 nitrogen 在 1790 年代出现，随新化学的传播音译了法语术语。在此以前，这种气体被称作「脱燃素空气」或「毒气」。

items.en: Once the element rather than the compound became the unit of chemistry, nitrogen named element 7 and its compounds were renamed as nitrides, nitrates and oxides.
items.cn: 当化学的单位从化合物转为元素后，nitrogen 成为 7 号元素的名称，其化合物则改称氮化物、硝酸盐与氧化物。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation is uncertain, and whether Chaptal or a colleague first suggested the form nitrogene is debated; Greek nitron itself has no agreed deeper origin.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语首见的确切书证年代存疑，nitrogene 这一形式由夏普塔尔还是其同僚最先提出仍有争议；希腊 nitron 本身的更深来源也无定论。

note.en: The first group holds words sharing the nitre root whose chemistry differs sharply; the second holds other atmospheric gases that are often confused with nitrogen.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「硝石」词根但化学性质差别很大的词；第二组是常与氮混淆的其他大气气体。

entries.definition: A salt or ester of nitric acid, containing the NO3 group, such as potassium nitrate in fertiliser. Nitrogen is the element; nitrate is one of its compounds.
entries.definitionCN: 硝酸的盐或酯，含 NO₃ 基团，如肥料中的硝酸钾。nitrogen 是元素，nitrate 是它的化合物之一。

entries.definition: A salt containing the NO2 group, used in cured meat and formed in soil as an intermediate step of nitrification.
entries.definitionCN: 含 NO₂ 基团的盐，用于腌肉，也在土壤中作为硝化过程的中间产物生成。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'containing nitrogen', as in nitrogenous waste. It describes a material, not the element itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「含氮的」的形容词，如含氮废物。它描述材料，而不是元素本身。

entries.definition: The gas that makes up about a fifth of the air and supports combustion and respiration. Nitrogen dilutes it and does not burn.
entries.definitionCN: 约占空气五分之一、支持燃烧与呼吸的气体。氮稀释它，且自身不燃烧。

entries.definition: A noble gas making up about one percent of the air, even less reactive than nitrogen. It is used where an absolutely inert atmosphere is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 约占空气百分之一的稀有气体，比氮更不活泼。需要绝对惰性气氛时就用它。

entries.definition: NH3, a pungent gas made industrially from nitrogen and hydrogen. It is the form in which nitrogen is turned into fertiliser.
entries.definitionCN: NH₃，工业上用氮与氢合成的刺激性气体。它正是氮被转化为肥料时所采取的形态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek nitron 'nitre' + -genes 'producer': the nitre-former, a name kept from a chemical claim.
normal.cn: 希腊 nitron「硝石」+ -genes「产生者」：成硝石者，一个源自化学主张的名字。

normal.en: The family runs nitrogenous, nitrate, nitrite, nitrify, denitrify and nitrogenase.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 nitrogenous、nitrate、nitrite、nitrify、denitrify、nitrogenase。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: nitrogen fixation, nitrogen cycle, liquid nitrogen, nitrogen oxides.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：固氮、氮循环、液氮、氮氧化物。

normal.en: Air is about four fifths nitrogen and one fifth oxygen.
normal.cn: 空气约五分之四是氮，五分之一是氧。

normal.en: Legumes fix nitrogen through root nodules, which is why farmers rotate them.
normal.cn: 豆科植物靠根瘤固氮，这也是农户进行轮作的原因。

abstract.en: Picture a bag of crisps puffed up with a gas that keeps every chip crisp.
abstract.cn: 想象一袋薯片鼓鼓的，里面充着一种让每片都保持酥脆的气体。

abstract.en: Picture a root nodule sliced open, pink inside, quietly turning air into soil fertility.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗根瘤被切开，内部粉红，正悄悄把空气变成土壤肥力。

abstract.en: Picture white vapour pouring off liquid nitrogen and rolling across the laboratory bench.
abstract.cn: 想象液氮上方涌出白色雾气，沿着实验台漫开。

examples.en: Nitrogen makes up roughly seventy-eight percent of the atmosphere.
examples.cn: 氮约占大气的百分之七十八。

examples.en: Excess nitrogen runoff from farms feeds algal blooms downstream.
examples.cn: 农场过量的氮径流在下游催生藻华。

examples.en: The welding shop uses nitrogen to purge oxygen from the pipes.
examples.cn: 焊接车间用氮把管道中的氧排净。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nitro（硝石）+ gen（产生）」——从硝石中得来的元素 → nitrogen 氮

root: 希腊 nitron「天然碱、硝石」+ -genes「产生者」→ 法语 nitrogene（1790，夏普塔尔）→ 英语 nitrogen。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one element from the periodic table through air, soil, protein, coolant, smog and the nitrogen cycle, ending with the naming claim that still sits inside the word.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让同一个元素从周期表走进空气、土壤、蛋白质、冷却剂、烟雾与氮循环，最后落在仍留在词里的那个命名主张上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a colourless gas everywhere and a sliced pink root nodule.
core.cn: 核心意象：无处不在的无色气体，与一颗切开的粉色根瘤。

branches.en: THE ATOM: element 7 is defined by seven protons and its triple bond.
branches.cn: 原子：7 号元素由七个质子与三键定义。

branches.en: THE BULK GAS: inertness is a property, so packaging and welding value it for what it does not do.
branches.cn: 主体气体：惰性本身即特性，包装与焊接看重的正是它「不做什么」。

branches.en: THE CYCLE: soil fertility and global circulation describe the same element changing form.
branches.cn: 循环：土壤肥力与全球循环描述的是同一元素不断变换形态。

branches.en: LIFE: amino acids and DNA make nitrogen a marker of living matter.
branches.cn: 生命：氨基酸与 DNA 使氮成为生命物质的标记。

branches.en: USES AND CLAIMS: liquid coolant, polluting oxides and the nitre story all hang off the same name.
branches.cn: 用途与说法：液氮冷却、污染性氧化物与硝石故事，都挂在同一个名字上。

intro.en: Nitrogen is a scientific compound of a Greek noun for nitre and a Greek suffix for producing, reshaped in French and then borrowed into English.
intro.cn: nitrogen 是科学造词：希腊语表示硝石的名词加希腊语表示产生的后缀，经法语改写后借入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin nitrum carried the nitre sense, and New Latin nitrogenium fixed the element name so that nitrate, nitrite and nitride could be built from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 nitrum 承载了「硝石」义，新拉丁语 nitrogenium 固定了元素名，使 nitrate、nitrite 与 nitride 得以由它构成。

definition_zh: 点头；点头示意；打盹；致意
definition_en: to move the head quickly down and up as a greeting or sign of agreement, and also to fall asleep briefly
core_image: 下巴向下一沉，又立刻弹回原位
scene: 散会后，他没有开口，只朝门口等着的同事低了下头，随即转身离开。He gave her a brief nod and walked out of the room.
sceneCN: 这里 nod 是「点头示意」（第 1 个义项：以点头表示问候或同意）；句意为他朝她轻轻点了下头，就走出了房间。图中可辨识物件：半开的会议室门、走廊里的同事、手里的文件。

derivatives.zh: nod 加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「点头的；（花枝等）低垂的」
nod 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er，义为「点头的人」

senses.title: To move the head down and up as a greeting or sign of agreement
senses.definition: to move the head quickly down and up, especially to greet someone or to show that you agree
senses.definitionCN: 快速地把头低下再抬起，尤用于问候别人或表示同意
senses.example: She nodded when I asked whether she agreed.
senses.exampleCN: 我问她是否同意时，她点了点头。
senses.why: A nod is the smallest visible yes: the head dips and returns, and the whole body quietly accepts what has just been said.
senses.whyCN: 点头是最小的一个看得见的「是」：头低下去又回来，整个身体就安静地接受了刚才听到的话。

senses.title: To fall asleep briefly, especially when you should stay awake
senses.definition: to begin to sleep accidentally for a short time, often while sitting or listening
senses.definitionCN: 在不该睡的时候不小心睡着一小会儿，常发生在坐着或听讲时
senses.example: He nodded off during the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 他在讲座中打起了瞌睡。
senses.why: The same drooping motion that signals sleepiness ends in a real loss of attention, so the verb stretches from a greeting to a head that falls forward and stays down.
senses.whyCN: 同一个耷拉下去的动作本是困意的信号，最后却变成真正的走神，于是词义从问候扩到「头垂下去、撑不住睡着」。

senses.title: A single quick movement of the head
senses.definition: a single quick movement of the head down and back up, used as a signal
senses.definitionCN: 头快速低下再抬起的一次动作，用作某种信号
senses.example: She answered with a quick nod.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻轻点了一下头作为回答。
senses.why: When the gesture is seen as an event rather than an act, the same word becomes a noun that counts each dip of the head.
senses.whyCN: 当这个手势被看成一件发生的事，而不是一个动作时，同一个词就变成名词，数得清每一次低头。

senses.title: An act of acknowledgement or tribute
senses.definition: a gesture, design or remark that openly acknowledges or honours someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 公开表示认可或致敬的动作、设计或言辞
senses.example: The new building is a nod to the town's fishing past.
senses.exampleCN: 这座新建筑是在向小镇的渔业历史致意。
senses.why: A small gesture of recognition is enough to say that something deserves respect, so the word widens from the head movement to any quiet sign of approval.
senses.whyCN: 一个很小的致意动作，就足以说明某样东西值得尊重；于是词义从头部的动作扩展到任何安静的认可。

intro.en: Nod is first recorded in Middle English, and its deeper origin is uncertain; it is generally treated as an expressive gesture word rather than a borrowing from Latin.
intro.cn: nod 最早记录于中古英语，更早的来源不确定；一般认为它是模仿动作的表达性词语，而不是借自拉丁语。

items.en: The verb appears first in Middle English, and no reliable older root has been established; most dictionaries mark its origin as uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词最早出现在中古英语，没有可靠的更早词根被确认；多数词典都标注其来源不确定。

items.en: Nodden meant to make a quick bowing movement of the head, close to the modern gesture.
items.cn: nodden 意为把头快速低一下，和现代的手势已经很接近。

items.en: The word is attested in writing from the fourteenth century with the sense of the head movement.
items.cn: 这个词从十四世纪起见于书面记录，表示头部的这一动作。

items.en: The phrase nod off appears for falling asleep in a chair, adding the sleep sense to the family.
items.cn: nod off 这个说法出现，用于在椅子上睡着，为这个词族添上了「打盹」的义项。

items.en: Modern English keeps the verb, uses the noun for the gesture, and extends a nod to to mean tribute.
items.cn: 现代英语保留动词，用名词指这个动作，并把 a nod to 扩展为致敬之意。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on nod, plus one word that only looks similar; the near-meaning group gathers other small signals and other words for light sleep.
note.cn: 形近组收由 nod 构成的形式，另收一个只是长得像的词；近义组收其他细小的示意动作，以及表示浅睡的词。

entries.definition: The present participle and adjective of nod, also used of drooping plants.
entries.definitionCN: nod 的现在分词兼形容词，也用于花枝低垂。

entries.definition: A person who nods, often repeatedly.
entries.definitionCN: 点头的人，常指反复点头的人。

entries.definition: An old informal word for the head; it only looks like nod and has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 「脑袋」的古老口语说法；只是拼写与 nod 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To bend the upper body forward as a greeting or sign of respect.
entries.definitionCN: 上身向前弯，表示问候或敬意。

entries.definition: To signal to someone with a movement of the hand or head.
entries.definitionCN: 用手或头的动作示意某人过来。

entries.definition: To sleep lightly for a short time.
entries.definitionCN: 浅浅地睡一小会儿。

entries.definition: A short sleep, usually planned, during the day.
entries.definitionCN: 白天的小睡，通常是有意安排的。

normalIntro.en: The word is probably an expressive gesture word, and its family keeps circling small head movements, approval and sudden sleep.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词很可能是模仿动作的表达性词语；词族始终围绕头部的细微动作、许可以及突然的睡意。

normal.en: A nod is one dip and return, unlike a bow, which bends the whole upper body.
normal.cn: 点头只是一次低头再抬起，与弯下整个上身的鞠躬不同。

normal.en: The past form doubled the final consonant: nod becomes nodded, not noded.
normal.cn: 过去式要双写词尾辅音：nod 变成 nodded，不是 noded。

normal.en: Nod off stretches the gesture into sleep, as if the head dips and never comes back.
normal.cn: nod off 把这个动作拖成了睡眠，好像头低下去就再没抬回来。

normal.en: Get the nod means to be approved or chosen, because approval was once given with a silent nod.
normal.cn: get the nod 表示获准或被选中，因为过去常以一个无声的点头表示同意。

normal.en: A nod to is figurative: the head gesture becomes a sign of respect for something old.
normal.cn: a nod to 是比喻用法：点头这个动作变成了对旧事物的尊重。

abstract.en: A gesture too small for words carries a complete yes, which is why nodding survives in every crowded room.
abstract.cn: 一个小到不需要言语的动作，却承载了完整的「是」，所以点头在每个拥挤的房间里都还活着。

abstract.en: The same downward motion marks both politeness and exhaustion, and the language keeps both in one word.
abstract.cn: 同一个向下的动作，既表示礼貌，也表示疲惫，而语言把它俩留在同一个词里。

abstract.en: Nod is the body answering before the mouth has decided what to say.
abstract.cn: nod 是身体在嘴巴想好说什么之前，先替它作了回答。

examples.en: She nodded when I asked whether she agreed.
examples.cn: 我问她是否同意时，她点了点头。

examples.en: He nodded off during the lecture.
examples.cn: 他在讲座中打起了瞌睡。

examples.en: The director gave the young actor the nod.
examples.cn: 导演点头选中了那位年轻演员。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a quick dip of the head; the senses then branch into agreement, the counted gesture, brief sleep and figurative tribute.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是头快速地向下一沉；义项由此分出同意、可数的手势、短暂入睡，以及比喻性的致意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the chin drops and springs straight back to where it was.
core.cn: 核心意象：下巴向下一沉，又立刻弹回原位。

branches.en: a head dipping in greeting
branches.cn: 问好时轻轻低下的头

branches.cn: 下巴抵在胸前的样子

branches.en: a greeting and the gesture that carries it
branches.cn: 问候与承载问候的那个动作

senses.definition: A loud or unpleasant sound
senses.definitionCN: 响亮刺耳的声音

senses.exampleCN: 噪声震得耳朵疼。

senses.whyCN: 古法语 noise 指争吵喧闹，英语保留吵闹义。

senses.title: Any sound heard

definition_en: words or ideas that have no meaning or logic; foolish behaviour or a silly plan; something absurd or worthless; also a style of writing that plays with meaningless language
core_image: 一张纸上写满歪歪扭扭的字，读出声却一句也讲不通

senses.title: Words that make no sense
senses.definition: spoken or written words that have no meaning or logic
senses.definitionCN: 说出的或写下的话语没有任何意义或逻辑
senses.example: What he said was nonsense from beginning to end.
senses.exampleCN: 他从头到尾说的都是废话。
senses.why: The word joins a negative prefix to the noun for meaning, so its first job is to mark language that carries no sense at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把否定前缀接到表示意义的名词上，所以它最初的本职就是标记完全不带意义的语言。

senses.title: Foolish behaviour or a silly plan
senses.definition: behaviour or a plan that is silly and should not be taken seriously
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢且不值得当真的行为或计划
senses.example: The idea of painting the roof at midnight was pure nonsense.
senses.exampleCN: 半夜去刷屋顶这个主意纯属胡闹。
senses.why: Once words are judged empty, the same judgement passes to actions, because a plan that makes no sense is exactly what the word already rejects.
senses.whyCN: 一旦话被判定为空，同一把尺子就量到行动上，因为讲不通的计划正是这个词本来要否定的东西。

senses.title: Something absurd or worthless
senses.titleCN: 荒唐的事；毫无价值的东西
senses.definition: a thing or situation so absurd that it seems unworthy of serious attention
senses.definitionCN: 荒唐到似乎不值得认真对待的事物或局面
senses.example: The whole ceremony struck the villagers as nonsense.
senses.exampleCN: 整场仪式在村民看来荒唐得很。
senses.why: The noun can point at the thing rather than at the talk, so anything that looks pointless can be labelled with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词可以不指话语而指事情本身，于是任何看起来没有意义的东西都能用同一个词来贴标签。

senses.title: A literary style built on meaningless words
senses.definition: a kind of writing, especially verse, that uses invented or meaningless words for comic or musical effect
senses.definitionCN: 一种使用生造词或无意义词以取得诙谐或音乐效果的文体，尤指诗歌
senses.example: The children loved the nonsense verse more than the serious poems.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们喜欢那些荒诞诗胜过严肃的诗。
senses.why: Nonsense can be made on purpose, and writers turned the defect into a genre, keeping the word while changing its purpose from blame to delight.
senses.whyCN: 无意义的东西也可以被故意造出来，作家把这个缺陷变成一种文体，词没有变，用途却从责备转成了取乐。

intro.en: Nonsense is a Latin prefix and a Latin noun joined in English, so it says on its surface exactly what it means.
intro.cn: nonsense 是一个拉丁前缀和一个拉丁名词在英语里拼合而成，字面上就把它自己的意思说了出来。

items.en: The negative particle non meant not, and Latin already used it to deny the word that followed.
items.cn: 否定小词 non 意为「不」，拉丁语中已用它来否定后面的词。

items.en: Sensus meant feeling, perception or meaning, and it came from the verb sentire, to feel.
items.cn: sensus 意为感觉、感知或意义，出自动词 sentire（感觉）。

items.en: English fixed the borrowed prefix to the borrowed noun, and the new word plainly announced no sense.
items.cn: 英语把借来的前缀固定在借来的名词上，新词直白地宣告「没有意义」。

items.en: Dictionaries generally date the noun to the early seventeenth century, when it first named foolish talk.
items.cn: 一般认为这个名词起于十七世纪初，最初指愚蠢的言谈。

items.en: Modern English extends it to foolish behaviour, absurd things and a playful literary style.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到荒唐行为、荒谬事物以及一种戏谑的文体。

normal.en: The word is non plus sense, a negative prefix fixed to the noun for meaning.
normal.cn: 这个词是 non 加 sense：一个否定前缀接在表示意义的名词上。

normal.en: Sensus in Latin meant perception as well as meaning, so the word denies sensible feeling along with sense.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 sensus 既指感知也指意义，所以这个词否定的既是意义，也是合乎情理的感觉。

normal.en: The prefix non- stays productive in English, which is why forms such as nonissue appear so easily.
normal.cn: 前缀 non- 在英语里一直能产，所以像 nonissue 这样的形式很容易冒出来。

normal.en: Nonsense verse is a real genre, so the word can name a deliberate art and not only a mistake.
normal.cn: nonsense verse 是一种真实存在的文体，可见这个词既指错误，也能指刻意的艺术。

normal.en: No-nonsense as an adjective means practical and unwilling to waste time, a reversal of the noun's reputation.
normal.cn: no-nonsense 作形容词指务实、不肯浪费时间，正好把这名词的名声翻了个面。

abstract.en: A word that says no sense needs no metaphor, because its two parts already perform the judgement.
abstract.cn: 一个说「没有意义」的词不需要比喻，它的两个构件本身就已经做出了判断。

abstract.en: The same label serves for empty talk, foolish acts and a comic art, since all three begin by refusing meaning.
abstract.cn: 同一个标签能用于空话、蠢事和一种诙谐艺术，因为三者都从拒绝意义开始。

abstract.en: Its playful fourth sense shows that a defect can be cultivated until it becomes a style.

definition_zh: 规范；准则；常态；标准；平均值
definition_en: a standard, rule, or usual pattern by which things are measured or judged
core_image: 木匠手里的直角尺：所有木板都要与它对齐
scene: 这里指「规范」。 A carpenter lays a steel square on a plank and uses it as the norm for every corner he cuts.
sceneCN: 这里 norm 是「量度所依的规矩、标准」（第 1 个义项：用来量度和判断的准则）；句意：木匠把钢制直角尺放在木板上，把它当作每个转角的准则，切割前逐一比对。图中可辨识物件：直角尺、木板、铅笔线、锯子、木屑。

senses.title: The Carpenter's Square: the rule things are measured against
senses.titleCN: 木工尺：万物对齐的规矩
senses.definition: a standard, pattern, or model used to measure or judge something
senses.definitionCN: 用来量度或判断事物的标准、范式或模型
senses.example: The team treated the first drawing as the norm for every later copy.
senses.exampleCN: 团队把最初的图纸当作此后每一份复制品的标准。
senses.why: Latin norma was the carpenter's square, the tool that tests whether a corner is true. From the tool itself came the abstract sense 'a rule or model to measure by', the sense Coleridge recorded in 1821.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 norma 是木工尺，用来检验角是否方正。从这件工具直接引出抽象义“量度所依的规矩或范式”，也就是柯勒律治 1821 年记录的那个义项。

senses.title: What Most People Do: the usual pattern
senses.titleCN: 多数人的做法：惯常模式
senses.definition: the usual or typical way of behaving, especially when most people accept it
senses.definitionCN: 通常或典型的行为方式，尤指多数人接受的方式
senses.example: In this office, arriving before nine has become the norm.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个办公室，九点前到岗已成为常态。
senses.why: Once a rule is shared, whatever follows it repeatedly looks like the rule in action. The standard becomes the ordinary case, so norm comes to mean the usual pattern.
senses.whyCN: 一旦规矩被共享，反复照着它做的样子就像是规矩本身在运行。标准于是变成普通情形，norm 也就有了“惯常模式”义。

senses.title: An Unwritten Law: a group's shared expectation
senses.titleCN: 不成文法：群体共享的期待
senses.definition: an accepted standard of behaviour that a group expects its members to follow
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体期待成员遵守的、被认可的行为标准
senses.example: Every culture has norms about how close you may stand when talking.
senses.exampleCN: 每种文化都有关于交谈时能站多近的规范。
senses.why: The measuring square is social here: the group lays it against each member's conduct. What fits the square is approved; what falls outside is deviant.
senses.whyCN: 这里的尺子是社会的：群体把它贴在每个成员的行为上。对齐尺子的被认可，偏离尺子的被视为越轨。

senses.title: The Average Line: a statistical norm
senses.definition: the average or typical level of a measured quantity in a population
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中某项被测数量的平均或典型水平
senses.example: The test scores were compared with the national norm for that age group.
senses.exampleCN: 这些测验分数与同年龄组的全国常模作了比较。
senses.why: Statistics draws one line through many scattered measurements. That line is the measure of the group, so the old 'rule' becomes the average value.
senses.whyCN: 统计学在许多散乱的测量值中画出一条线。这条线就是群体的量度，于是古老的“规矩”变成平均值。

senses.title: The Line Others Must Meet: a benchmark
senses.definition: a level of performance or achievement used as a standard for comparison
senses.definitionCN: 用作比较标准的表现或成就水平
senses.example: Her time in the race set a new norm for the club.
senses.exampleCN: 她的比赛用时为俱乐部立下了新的基准。
senses.why: If the square decides what counts as straight, it also decides what counts as good enough. A measured result can therefore be held up as the norm others must match.
senses.whyCN: 如果尺子决定什么算直，它也就决定什么算达标。因此一个测得的成绩可以被举为他人必须对齐的基准。

senses.title: Size in Mathematics: the length of a vector
senses.titleCN: 数学中的大小：向量的模
senses.definition: in mathematics, a function that assigns a size or length to a vector or a space
senses.definitionCN: 数学中为向量或空间指定大小、长度的函数
senses.example: The norm of the vector is the square root of the sum of its squared components.
senses.exampleCN: 这个向量的模是其各分量平方和的平方根。
senses.why: Mathematics keeps the oldest meaning most literally: a norm is the rule that tells you how large an object is. Size itself is measured by that rule.
senses.whyCN: 数学最字面地保留了最古老的含义：norm 就是告诉你一个对象有多大的那把尺。大小由这把尺来量。

senses.title: The Accepted Way of Speaking: a linguistic standard
senses.titleCN: 被认可的说话方式：语言规范
senses.definition: the standard form of a language, or the accepted usage in a community of speakers
senses.definitionCN: 语言的标准形式，或某个说话群体中被认可的用法
senses.example: Dictionaries record usage; they do not always prescribe the norm.
senses.exampleCN: 词典记录用法，并不总是规定规范。
senses.why: Language also has a straight edge: grammar and spelling are checked against an accepted pattern. What fits that pattern is called the norm.
senses.whyCN: 语言也有一把直尺：语法和拼写要对着被认可的范式检查。符合这个范式的就叫规范。

senses.title: A Rule of Conduct: the ethical norm
senses.definition: a principle of right conduct that guides or judges moral behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 指导或评判道德行为的正当行为原则
senses.example: The ethical norm of informed consent shapes modern medical research.
senses.exampleCN: 知情同意的伦理规范塑造了现代医学研究。
senses.why: The social square becomes a moral one: actions are laid against a principle and judged straight or crooked. That principle is the norm.
senses.whyCN: 社会的尺子变成道德的尺子：行为被放在原则旁边，判为端直或歪斜。这条原则就是规范。

senses.title: The Fixed Specification: a technical standard
senses.definition: an official or technical specification that a product or process must meet
senses.definitionCN: 产品或流程必须达到的官方或技术规格
senses.example: The bolts were manufactured to a norm agreed by the industry.
senses.exampleCN: 这些螺栓按行业商定的标准制造。
senses.why: In industry the measuring tool becomes written down: the rule is fixed in numbers so that every copy matches. The norm is then a specification.
senses.whyCN: 在工业里，量具被写成了文字：规矩固定为数字，让每一件复制品都对齐。此时 norm 就是规格。

intro.en: Norm entered English in 1821 through French from Latin norma, the carpenter's square. The tool's name became the abstract word for a standard, while norma's deeper origin is unknown.
intro.cn: norm 于 1821 年经法语从拉丁语 norma（木工尺）进入英语。工具的名字变成了 abstract 意义上的“标准”，而 norma 更深层的来源不明。

items.en: Latin norma was already used in English for a carpenter's square; in the 18th century Lacaille also gave the name Norma to a small southern constellation.
items.cn: 拉丁语 norma 在 17 世纪 70 年代已被英语用来指木工尺；18 世纪拉卡伊还把 Norma 用作南天一个小星座的名字。

items.en: Coleridge records norm in the sense 'a standard, pattern, or model', borrowed from French norme.
items.cn: 柯勒律治记录 norm 表示“标准、范式、模型”，借自法语 norme。

items.en: French norme 'standard, rule' is the immediate borrowing path from Latin to English.
items.cn: 法语 norme“标准、规矩”是这个词从拉丁语进入英语的直接通道。

items.en: Latin norma meant 'carpenter's square, rule, pattern' and supplied both the tool and the abstract rule.
items.cn: 拉丁语 norma 意为“木工尺、规矩、范式”，同时提供了工具义和抽象的规矩义。

items.en: Norma's own origin is unknown. Klein suggested it came through Etruscan from Greek gnomon 'carpenter's square, judge', but that is a suggestion, not a settled fact.
items.cn: norma 本身的来源不明。Klein 认为它经伊特鲁里亚语借自希腊语 gnomon“木工尺、判者”，但这只是一种说法，并非定论。

items.en: The norma family spreads into normal, normalize, normative, abnormal and enormous, while norm itself stays the bare noun for a standard.
items.cn: norma 词族扩展到 normal、normalize、normative、abnormal、enormous，而 norm 本身仍是表示“标准”的光秃名词。

note.en: The first group keeps words that look or sound like norm; the second keeps words that share part of its meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是词形或读音相近的词，第二组是部分词义相近的词。

entries.definition: the Latin word for a carpenter's square, also the name of a small southern constellation. It is the source of norm, not a variant spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示“木工尺”的词，也是南天一个小星座的名字。它是 norm 的来源，而不是异体拼写。

entries.definition: the adjective built from norm, meaning conforming to the usual standard.
entries.definitionCN: 由 norm 构成的形容词，表示“合乎通常标准的”。

entries.definition: built from ex- plus norma, literally 'out of rule'; it means very large, not standard.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ex- 加 norma 构成，字面是“出了规矩”；意思是“巨大”，而不是“标准”。

entries.definition: an agreed level or rule, often written down. Norm may be unwritten, statistical, or simply customary.
entries.definitionCN: 商定的水平或规则，常写成条文。norm 可以是不成文的、统计的，或只是习惯性的。

entries.definition: a customary way accepted by a group. It is closer to social norms than to measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 群体接受的惯常做法。它更接近“社会规范”，而与量度关系较远。

entries.definition: the typical middle value. It covers only the statistical sense of norm.
entries.definitionCN: 典型的中间值。它只覆盖 norm 的统计学义项。

normalIntro.en: Real links only: the Latin tool norma, the norm family, and fixed English phrases that keep the measuring image alive.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实联系：拉丁语工具 norma、norm 词族，以及保留“量度”意象的固定英语短语。

normal.en: Norma is Latin for a carpenter's square, the tool that checks a right angle.
normal.cn: norma 在拉丁语里是木工尺，用来检验直角。

normal.en: Norm, normal, abnormal and enormous all carry norma; enormous adds ex- 'out of'.
normal.cn: norm、normal、abnormal、enormous 都带着 norma；enormous 还加了 ex-“出”。

normal.en: 'The norm' is the standard case, and 'normal' is what conforms to it.
normal.cn: the norm 是标准情形，normal 则是合乎它的东西。

normal.en: 'Social norms' are the unwritten rules a group expects its members to follow.
normal.cn: social norms 是一个群体期待成员遵守的不成文规则。

normal.en: 'Set the norm' and 'deviate from the norm' are fixed frames that keep the measuring image alive.
normal.cn: set the norm 与 deviate from the norm 是固定搭配，让“量尺”的意象一直活着。

abstract.en: Picture a steel square pressed against a plank: the edge either matches or it does not.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钢尺贴在木板上：边要么对齐，要么没对齐。

abstract.en: Now press the same square against a crowd's behaviour: approval and disapproval are the two sides of the edge.
abstract.cn: 再把同一把尺贴到人群的行为上：认可与不认可就是尺边的两侧。

abstract.en: In statistics the square shrinks to a single line drawn through a cloud of dots.
abstract.cn: 在统计学里，这把尺缩成穿过一片散点的一条线。

examples.en: Working from home has become the norm in many software companies.
examples.cn: 居家办公在许多软件公司已成为常态。

examples.en: Each laboratory sets its own norms for handling samples.
examples.cn: 每个实验室都有自己的样品处理规范。

examples.en: Her results were far above the norm for students at that level.
examples.cn: 她的成绩远高于该水平学生的基准。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺姆」——木匠点头说“诺”，姆指一量，全按这把尺来 → norm 规范、标准

root: 拉丁语 norma“木工尺、规矩、标准”，经法语 norme 进入英语；norma 更深来源不确定，一般认为经伊特鲁里亚语借自希腊语 gnōmōn。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of norm grow from one tool: the carpenter's square. The square first measures wood, then behaviour, then language, then numbers, until 'the norm' means whatever a group or a curve treats as the standard line.
sensesIntro.cn: norm 的九个义项都从一件工具长出来：木工尺。这把尺先量木头，再量行为、语言和数字，最后 the norm 指群体或曲线所认定的那条标准线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carpenter's square laid against a plank.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把贴在木板上的木工直角尺。

branches.en: THE RULE ITSELF: the square as a model, and a measured result held up as a benchmark.
branches.cn: 规矩本身：作为范式的尺子，以及被举为基准的测量成绩。

branches.en: HABIT AND SOCIETY: what most people do, and what a group expects its members to do.
branches.cn: 习惯与社会：多数人的做法，以及群体对成员的期待。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: the statistical average and the mathematical size of a vector.
branches.cn: 量度：统计平均值与数学中向量的大小。

branches.en: LANGUAGE AND MORALS: accepted usage, and a principle of right conduct.
branches.cn: 语言与道德：被认可的用法，以及正当行为的原则。

branches.en: SPECIFICATION: the rule written down as a technical standard.
branches.cn: 规格：把规矩写下来，成为技术标准。

intro.en: Norm is the bare Latin noun norma used in English. Its family grows by ordinary suffixes and by prefixes such as ab- and ex-, all built on the same measuring tool.
intro.cn: norm 就是拉丁语名词 norma 原样进入英语。它的词族靠普通后缀以及 ab-、ex- 等前缀扩展，全部建在同一件量具上。

latinIntro.en: Latin norma 'carpenter's square, rule' is the source; normalis 'in conformity with rule' and enormis 'out of rule' are its two Latin branches. Norma's deeper origin is uncertain, possibly through Etruscan from Greek gnomon.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 norma“木工尺、规矩”是源头；normalis“合乎规矩”与 enormis“出了规矩”是它的两条拉丁分支。norma 更深来源不确定，可能经伊特鲁里亚语来自希腊语 gnomon。

items.meaningCN: 标准；惯常模式（拉丁名词原样进入英语）
items.example: Flexible hours are now the norm.
items.exampleCN: 弹性工时如今已是常态。

items.meaningCN: 正常的；合乎通常标准的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The nurse said the readings were normal.
items.exampleCN: 护士说各项读数都正常。

items.meaningCN: 通常；按常规方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The train normally arrives at eight.
items.exampleCN: 这趟列车通常八点到。

items.meaningCN: 使标准化；使正常化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The two sides agreed to normalize trade.
items.exampleCN: 双方同意使贸易正常化。

items.meaning: the process of making normal or standard
items.meaningCN: 正常化；标准化（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Data normalization put the scores on one scale.
items.exampleCN: 数据归一化把各项分数放到同一尺度上。

items.meaningCN: 规范的；标准性的（-ative 构成形容词）
items.example: The report mixes descriptive and normative claims.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告把描述性主张与规范性主张混在一起。

items.meaningCN: 无规范的；缺少准则的（-less 表示“没有”）
items.example: A normless market makes prices hard to judge.
items.exampleCN: 没有规范的市场让价格难以判断。

items.meaningCN: 异常的；偏离常规的（ab-“离开”+ normal）
items.example: An abnormal reading led to more tests.
items.exampleCN: 一项异常读数引来了更多检查。

items.meaningCN: 异常；反常之处（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The scan showed a slight abnormality.
items.exampleCN: 扫描显示有一处轻微异常。

items.meaning: literally out of rule; very large
items.meaningCN: 字面“出了规矩”；巨大的（e- 即 ex-“出”+ norm + -ous）
items.example: An enormous wave struck the pier.
items.exampleCN: 一道巨浪打上了码头。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 木工尺；规矩；标准（更深来源不确定）

latinEntries.meaning: in conformity with rule; made according to a square
latinEntries.meaningCN: 合乎规矩的；按木工尺做的
出了规矩的；不规则的；极大的

definition_zh: 正常的；标准的；正规的；垂直的；常态；法线
definition_en: conforming to an established rule or standard, and therefore usual, healthy, or perpendicular in geometry
core_image: 一块木板贴着木工尺：边与尺严丝合缝，没有偏斜
scene: 测量员把水平尺贴上新建的墙，检查每层砖是否与地面垂直。A surveyor holds a level against a newly built wall and checks that each course of bricks is normal to the ground.
sceneCN: 这里 normal 是「合乎规矩、端直无偏」（第 2 个义项：几何上与基准成直角）；句意：测量员把水平仪贴在一堵新建的墙上，检查每一层砖都与地面垂直。图中可辨识物件：水平仪、新墙、砖缝、安全帽、卷尺；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 常态；正常状态；（几何）法线

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 常态；正常状态（多用于美式英语）

senses.title: The Square Says Yes: conforming to the rule
senses.definition: typical, common, or in accordance with an established standard
senses.definitionCN: 典型的、常见的，或符合既定标准的
senses.example: The machine was running at normal speed.
senses.exampleCN: 机器以正常速度运转。
senses.why: Late Latin normalis meant 'in conformity with rule' and classical Latin described something 'made according to a carpenter's square'. What the square accepts is normal; what it rejects is not.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 normalis 意为“合乎规矩”，古典拉丁语则指“按木工尺做成的”。尺子认可的就是 normal，尺子拒绝的就不是。

senses.title: The Right Angle: perpendicular in geometry
senses.definition: standing at a right angle to a line or surface, as a geometric relation
senses.definitionCN: 与一条线或一个面成直角，指几何关系
senses.example: The normal line meets the curve at exactly ninety degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 法线与曲线恰好成九十度相交。
senses.why: A carpenter's square exists to make right angles. The 1640s geometry sense simply states the tool's job in mathematical language: a normal line is square to the surface.
senses.whyCN: 木工尺存在的目的就是做出直角。17 世纪 40 年代的几何义只是用数学语言说出这件工具的职责：法线与面成直角。

senses.title: Business as Usual: the ordinary standard
senses.definition: conforming to common standards or the established order of things
senses.definitionCN: 符合通行标准或事物的既定秩序
senses.example: Normal service resumed after the power cut.
senses.exampleCN: 停电之后服务恢复正常。
senses.why: Once the square stands for the established order, anything that follows that order is normal. The 1828 sense generalizes the geometrical rule into everyday standards.
senses.whyCN: 当尺子代表既定秩序，任何顺着这个秩序的东西就是 normal。1828 年的义项把几何规矩推广为日常标准。

senses.title: Within the Healthy Range
senses.definition: healthy or functioning within the expected range, used of bodies and body readings
senses.definitionCN: 健康或在预期范围内运作，用于身体及各项读数
senses.example: Her blood pressure was normal for her age.
senses.exampleCN: 就她的年龄而言，血压正常。
senses.why: Medicine measures a body against a range taken from healthy people. A reading inside that range conforms to the rule, so it is called normal.
senses.whyCN: 医学用取自健康人群的范围来量身体。落在这个范围内的读数合乎规矩，于是被称作正常。

senses.title: The Bell Curve: statistically typical
senses.titleCN: 钟形曲线：统计上的典型
senses.definition: falling at or near the average of a statistical distribution
senses.definitionCN: 位于统计分布的均值处或附近
senses.example: Most measurements cluster around the normal value.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数测量值聚集在正常值附近。
senses.why: Statistics turns the rule into a curve: most cases pile up at the middle, and that middle is the normal value. Being near it is being typical.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把规矩变成一条曲线：多数个案堆在中间，中间就是正常值。靠近它就是典型。

senses.title: Nothing Special: ordinary and unremarkable
senses.titleCN: 没有什么特别：普通平常
senses.definition: ordinary and not special or surprising, used of events and days
senses.definitionCN: 普通、不特别也不令人意外的，用于事件和日子
senses.example: It was a normal Tuesday, with nothing unusual at all.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个平常的星期二，没有任何异常。
senses.why: The standard case is also the unexciting case. When nothing departs from the rule, the day is merely normal.
senses.whyCN: 标准情形也是不起眼的情形。当没有任何东西偏离规矩，这一天就只是 normal。

senses.title: Back to Normal: the usual state
senses.definition: the usual or expected state of affairs, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 通常或预期的事态，作名词使用
senses.example: After the storm, the town slowly returned to normal.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，小镇慢慢恢复了常态。
senses.why: The adjective was turned into a noun in 1890: 'the normal' is the state that conforms to the rule. To return to normal is to line up with the square again.
senses.whyCN: 1890 年形容词转为名词：the normal 就是合乎规矩的状态。return to normal 就是重新与尺子对齐。

senses.title: The Perpendicular Line: a geometric noun
senses.definition: a line or plane perpendicular to a given line, surface, or curve
senses.definitionCN: 与给定直线、平面或曲线垂直的线或面
senses.example: Drop a normal from the point to the base line.
senses.exampleCN: 从该点向基线作一条法线。
senses.why: The noun use of 1727 names the very line the square draws. A normal is the line that stands at a right angle, the geometric object behind the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 1727 年的名词用法命名的正是尺子画出的那条线。normal 就是那条成直角的线，是形容词背后的几何对象。

senses.title: The Standard-Setting School
senses.titleCN: 立标准的学校：师范学校
senses.definition: in normal school, a 19th-century teacher-training institution whose name meant 'setting the standard'
senses.definitionCN: normal school 指 19 世纪的师范学校，其名称理据是“用来设定标准的”
senses.example: The state opened its first normal school in 1839.
senses.exampleCN: 该州于 1839 年开办了第一所师范学校。
senses.why: Normal school was translated in 1835 from French école normale (1794). The school was named as the place that sets the standard for teachers, not as a place for 'ordinary' students.
senses.whyCN: normal school 于 1835 年译自法语 école normale（1794）。这所学校被命名为“为教师立标准的地方”，而不是“普通学生的地方”。

intro.en: Normal shares norma with norm, but it appeared much earlier and first meant 'conforming to rule' before it meant 'usual'. The geometrical sense came in the 1640s; the everyday sense 'standard, ordinary' is recorded in 1828.
intro.cn: normal 与 norm 同出 norma，但它出现得早得多，且先有“合乎规矩”义，后有“正常、通常”义。几何义出现于 17 世纪 40 年代；日常的“标准、普通”义记录于 1828 年。

items.en: First recorded with the sense 'typical, common', already applied to ordinary cases rather than to geometry.
items.cn: 最早记录的义项是“典型的、常见的”，已经用于普通情形，而不是几何。

items.en: The geometrical sense 'standing at a right angle, perpendicular' appears, drawing directly on the carpenter's square.
items.cn: 出现几何义“成直角的、垂直的”，直接取象于木工尺。

items.en: From Late Latin normalis 'in conformity with rule, normal'; in classical Latin the same word meant 'made according to a carpenter's square', from norma 'rule, pattern'.
items.cn: 来自晚期拉丁语 normalis“合乎规矩的、正常的”；古典拉丁语中这个词意为“按木工尺做成的”，出自 norma“规矩、范式”。

items.en: The sense 'conforming to common standards or established order' is recorded, possibly current earlier.
items.cn: 记录到“符合通行标准或既定秩序”的义项，可能在实际使用中更早。

items.en: Normal school is translated from French école normale (1794); the name means an institution that sets the standard.
items.cn: normal school 译自法语 école normale（1794）；这个名字的意思是“设定标准的机构”。

items.en: The noun 'normal state' is recorded in 1890, while the geometrical noun normal 'perpendicular line' dates from 1727. Both keep the image of a line drawn square to something.
items.cn: 名词“常态”记录于 1890 年，而几何名词 normal“垂直线”始于 1727 年。两者都保留了“与某物成直角的一条线”的意象。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the same norma family; the near-meaning group holds words that overlap with only part of normal.
note.cn: 形近组是同一个 norma 词族；近义组是只与 normal 部分义项重叠的词。

entries.definition: the standard itself. Normal is the adjective saying that something conforms to it.
entries.definitionCN: 标准本身。normal 是形容词，表示某物合乎这个标准。

entries.definition: prescribing what should be done, not describing what is usual. Normal describes fact; normative sets a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 规定应该怎么做，而不是描述通常怎样。normal 描述事实，normative 立规矩。

entries.definition: departing from the normal. The ab- prefix means 'away from', the exact opposite of conforming.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离正常的。前缀 ab- 意为“离开”，正是“合乎”的反面。

entries.definition: not special or unusual. It stresses lack of distinction, while normal stresses conformity to a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 不特别、不稀奇。它强调“不出众”，normal 强调“合乎标准”。

entries.definition: showing the usual qualities of a group. It points to a representative example, not to a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 体现某类事物通常特征的。它指向代表性样本，而不是规矩。

entries.definition: an established level or rule. It is the noun behind normal; normal is what meets that level.
entries.definitionCN: 既定的水平或规则。它是 normal 背后的名词；normal 就是达到该水平的。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: normal and norm both come from norma, the carpenter's square, and the geometry sense still shows the tool at work.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想是真实的：normal 与 norm 都出自 norma（木工尺），而几何义至今仍能看出这件工具在工作。

normal.en: Normalis in Late Latin meant 'in conformity with rule'; the rule was norma, the carpenter's square.
normal.cn: 晚期拉丁语 normalis 意为“合乎规矩”，而规矩就是 norma，那把木工尺。

normal.en: Normal and norm share norma, but normal is older and started from 'conforming to rule', not from 'usual'.
normal.cn: normal 与 norm 共用 norma，但 normal 更早，而且起点是“合乎规矩”，不是“通常”。

normal.en: In geometry a normal line is square to a surface: the tool's right angle turned into a line.
normal.cn: 几何中的法线与面成直角：工具的直角变成了一条线。

normal.en: Return to normal is a fixed phrase: the state that lines up with the square again.
normal.cn: return to normal 是固定说法：重新与尺子对齐的状态。

normal.en: A normal school was a standard-setting school for teachers, not a school for ordinary people.
normal.cn: normal school 是为教师立标准的学校，不是给普通人办的学校。

abstract.en: Picture a level on a wall: the bubble sits in the middle and the wall is declared true.
abstract.cn: 想象一把水平尺贴在墙上：气泡停在中间，这堵墙就被判为端正。

abstract.en: The same middle position becomes health: a reading inside the expected range is normal.
abstract.cn: 同一个中间位置变成健康：落在预期范围内的读数就是正常。

abstract.en: Move the frame to a crowd and the middle becomes the average person; normal is the crowd's centre line.
abstract.cn: 把框架移到人群，中间就成了平均人；normal 就是人群的中心线。

examples.en: Under normal circumstances, the ferry crosses the river every hour.
examples.cn: 正常情况下，渡轮每小时过河一次。

examples.en: The doctor said the results were normal and no treatment was needed.
examples.cn: 医生说结果正常，不需要治疗。

examples.en: It took three days for the airport to return to normal after the snow.
examples.cn: 大雪过后机场用了三天才恢复正常。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺默」——大家都点头应“诺”、默认照做 → normal 正常的、标准的

root: 拉丁语 normalis“合乎规矩的”，出自 norma“木工尺、规矩”；与 norm 同源，先有“合乎规矩”，后有“正常、通常”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of normal all come from one act: laying a square against something. Wood, walls, bodies, numbers and schools are each checked against a rule, and whatever fits is called normal.
sensesIntro.cn: normal 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：把尺子贴在某物上。木头、墙壁、身体、数字和学校都要对着规矩检查，对得上的就叫 normal。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a level or square laid against a surface, with no tilt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把水平尺或直角尺贴在表面上，没有倾斜。

branches.en: CONFORMITY: fitting the rule, then fitting the ordinary order of things.
branches.cn: 合乎：先合乎规矩，再合乎事物的日常秩序。

branches.en: GEOMETRY: the perpendicular direction and the perpendicular line itself.
branches.cn: 几何：垂直方向，以及垂直线本身。

branches.en: MEASURED BODIES AND NUMBERS: the healthy range and the centre of a distribution.
branches.cn: 被量度的身体与数字：健康范围与分布中心。

branches.en: THE UNREMARKABLE AND THE USUAL STATE: an ordinary day, and 'the normal' as a noun.
branches.cn: 平常与常态：普通的一天，以及名词 the normal。

branches.en: THE STANDARD-SETTING SCHOOL: normal school, named for the standard it sets.
branches.cn: 立标准的学校：normal school，因它所设定的标准而得名。

intro.en: Normal is norma plus the adjective suffix -alis, which becomes -al in English. The family then adds -ly, -ity, -ize and the negative prefix ab-.
intro.cn: normal 是 norma 加形容词后缀 -alis（进入英语作 -al）。词族随后再加 -ly、-ity、-ize 以及否定前缀 ab-。

latinIntro.en: Latin normalis 'in conformity with rule' comes from norma 'carpenter's square'. Its opposite branch is enormis 'out of rule', and the bare noun norma also gives English norm.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 normalis“合乎规矩”出自 norma“木工尺”。它的反义分支是 enormis“出了规矩”，而光秃名词 norma 也给了英语 norm。

items.meaningCN: 正常的；合乎通常标准的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Normal weather returned after the cold spell.
items.exampleCN: 寒潮过后恢复了正常天气。

items.meaningCN: 通常；正常地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: I normally walk to work.
items.exampleCN: 我通常走路上班。

items.meaningCN: 正常；常态（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The city slowly regained a sense of normality.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市慢慢恢复了常态感。

items.meaningCN: 使正常化；使标准化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The agreement aimed to normalize diplomatic ties.
items.exampleCN: 这项协议旨在使外交关系正常化。

items.meaningCN: 正常化；标准化（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Database normalization reduces repeated data.
items.exampleCN: 数据库规范化减少了重复数据。

items.meaningCN: 规范的；标准性的（-ative 构成形容词）
items.example: Normative grammar states how people should write.
items.exampleCN: 规范语法说明人们应该怎么写。

items.meaningCN: 异常的；不正常的（ab-“离开”+ normal）
items.example: The test found an abnormal rhythm in the heart.
items.exampleCN: 检查发现心律异常。

items.meaningCN: 异常；反常（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The technicians looked for any abnormality in the sample.
items.exampleCN: 技术人员检查样本中是否有异常。

items.meaningCN: 规范；常态（拉丁名词原样进入英语）
items.example: Late arrival is the norm on rainy days.
items.exampleCN: 下雨天迟到是常态。

items.meaning: literally out of rule; very large
items.meaningCN: 字面“出了规矩”；巨大的（e- 即 ex-“出”）
items.example: The stadium holds an enormous crowd.
items.exampleCN: 这座体育场能容纳极大的人群。

latinEntries.meaning: in conformity with rule; made according to a square
latinEntries.meaningCN: 合乎规矩的；按木工尺做成的
木工尺；规矩；标准（更深来源不确定）
出了规矩的；不规则的；极大的

definition_zh: 公证人；公证员
definition_en: a public officer who witnesses signatures and certifies documents so that others can rely on them
core_image: 一枚印章压在纸上：为这份文书的真实性留下一个被官方承认的标记
scene: 签授权书那天，双方请来一位公证人核对身份。On the day the power of attorney was signed, the parties asked a notary to check their identity.
sceneCN: 这里 notary 是「公证人」（第 1 个义项：依法见证签署并证明文书真实的公职人员）；句意：签授权书那天，双方请来公证人核对身份。

derivatives.zh: 由 notary 加形容词后缀 -ial 构成，义为「公证的；公证人的」
由 notary 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「对……办理公证；公证」
由 notarize 加 -ation 构成，义为「公证行为；公证手续」

senses.title: A public officer who certifies documents
senses.definition: a public officer, often a lawyer, who witnesses signatures and certifies the authenticity of documents
senses.definitionCN: 通常是律师的公职人员，见证签署并证明文书的真实性
senses.example: The deed was acknowledged before a notary public.
senses.exampleCN: 这份契据在公证人面前得到确认。
senses.why: Latin notarius was a clerk who wrote marks and records, and that office grew into a public certifier.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 notarius 本是把要点记成记号与文书的书记，这个职务后来长成替公众作证明的人。

senses.title: A civil-law officer who drafts and authenticates instruments
senses.definition: in civil-law countries, an officer with a legal monopoly to draft and authenticate contracts, wills, and other instruments
senses.definitionCN: 在大陆法系国家依法专职起草并认证合同、遗嘱等文书的官员
senses.example: In many civil-law countries a notary authenticates the sale of a house.
senses.exampleCN: 在许多大陆法系国家，公证人负责认证房屋买卖。
senses.why: The continental office kept the Latin clerk role and added a state-backed monopoly over formal deeds.
senses.whyCN: 欧洲大陆的公证职务保留了拉丁书记的写作职能，又加上国家对正式文书的专营授权，于是义项从「记录」偏向「起草并认证」。

senses.title: A clerk who writes records
senses.definition: historical: a clerk or secretary whose work was to write notes and keep records
senses.definitionCN: 历史上的书记员或秘书，工作是记下要点并保存档案
senses.example: The notary of the guild kept the minutes of every meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 行会的书记保存每次会议的记录。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply the person who writes marks and notes, before the office became a public trust.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项只是「写下记号与要点的人」，先有写字记录的人，才有后来被公众信任的证明职务。

intro.en: Notary goes back to Latin nota, a mark, and notarius, the clerk who wrote marks and notes.
intro.cn: notary 可追到拉丁语 nota（记号）与 notarius（写下记号与要点的书记）。

items.en: Nota means a mark, a sign, or a written character.
items.cn: nota 意为记号、标记或写下的字符。

items.en: Notare means to mark or note something down in writing.
items.cn: notare 意为作标记、把某事记下来。

items.en: Notarius is the clerk or shorthand writer who makes such marks.
items.cn: notarius 是作这类记号、速记要点的书记。

items.en: Notaire carries the office and the title into French.
items.cn: notaire 把这个职务与头衔带进法语。

items.en: Notarie names a clerk or a public writer in English records.
items.cn: 中古英语 notarie 指书记，也指受雇代写文书的人。

items.en: Notary public becomes the fixed title of the certifying officer.
items.cn: 现代英语中 notary public 成为这类证明官员的固定头衔。

note.en: Notary belongs to the Latin mark family and sits beside the words for sworn statements and formal proof.
note.cn: notary 属于拉丁语「标记」词族，与宣誓陈述和正式证明的词相邻。

entries.definition: relating to a notary or to notarization
entries.definitionCN: 与公证人或公证行为有关的

entries.definition: to have a document certified by a notary
entries.definitionCN: 由公证人对文书办理公证

entries.definition: a system of written marks or symbols
entries.definitionCN: 记号法；符号系统（同出 nota 一源）

entries.definition: a written statement sworn before an officer
entries.definitionCN: 在官员面前宣誓后作出的书面陈述；宣誓书

entries.definition: to witness and confirm something formally
entries.definitionCN: 正式见证并确认某事

entries.definition: to state officially that something is true or correct
entries.definitionCN: 官方证明某事真实或正确

normalIntro.en: Notary grows from Latin nota, a mark: the office began with the person who wrote marks and notes.
normalIntro.cn: notary 长自拉丁语 nota（记号）：这个职务最初就是写下记号与要点的人。

normal.en: Nota means a mark, and notarius was the clerk who wrote such marks.
normal.cn: nota 意为记号，notarius 就是写这类记号的书记。

normal.en: Notarial is the adjective and notarize is the verb of the same family.
normal.cn: notarial 是同族的形容词，notarize 是同族的动词。

normal.en: The full English title is notary public, not merely notary.
normal.cn: 英语里的完整头衔是「notary public」，而不只是 notary。

normal.en: A notary seal marks a document as certified.
normal.cn: 「notary seal」把一份文书标记为已公证。

normal.en: Civil-law notaries draft deeds as well as certify them.
normal.cn: 大陆法系的公证人既起草也认证契据。

abstract.en: A stamp presses a raised seal onto a sheet of paper, leaving a mark anyone can check.
abstract.cn: 一枚印章压出一圈凸起的印痕，留下人人可查的标记，对应第 1 个义项的证明职能。

abstract.en: An officer in a civil-law city reads a will aloud and signs it for the state.
abstract.cn: 大陆法系城市里，一位官员朗读遗嘱并代表国家签字，对应公证人的起草与认证职能。

abstract.en: A clerk with an ink pen writes down what was said, mark after mark.
abstract.cn: 一位书记用墨水笔把听到的话一行行记下，对应最古老的记录义项。

examples.en: The notary public certified the signature on the deed.
examples.cn: 公证人对契据上的签名作了认证。

examples.en: The parties signed the lease before a notary.
examples.cn: 双方在公证人面前签署了租约。

examples.en: The notary kept a copy of each act in the office.
examples.cn: 公证人在事务所里保存每一份文书的副本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺特瑞」——名字里带一个「诺」，一诺千金，由他在场替你作证；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 nota（记号、标记）→ notare（作标记）→ notarius（记录员、书记）→ 古法语 notaire → 英语 notary，核心义「作标记并把话记下来的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Notary begins as a clerk who writes marks, becomes the civil-law officer who drafts deeds, and in English settles as the public certifier of documents.
sensesIntro.cn: notary 先指写下记号的书记，再指大陆法系起草契据的官员，英语里最终落定为替公众认证文书的公证人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an official seal pressed onto a document to mark it as verified.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚公章压上文书，为它打上可核验的标记。

branches.en: The public certifier of signatures is the modern core sense.
branches.cn: 替公众认证签名，是现代最核心的义项。

branches.en: The civil-law officer adds drafting power to the certifying role.
branches.cn: 大陆法系公证人在认证之外又加上起草文书的权力。

branches.en: The historical clerk is the sense closest to the Latin source.
branches.cn: 历史上的书记义项，离拉丁语词源最近。

branches.en: Both senses are offices of writing, one public and one private.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是「与文字打交道」的职务，只是一个为公众、一个为私人。

branches.en: Both certify authenticity, but only the civil-law officer drafts the deed.
branches.cn: 两者都认证真实性，但只有大陆法系公证人亲自起草契据。

intro.en: Notary rests on the Latin mark family: nota, notare, notarius, with notarial and notarize built in English.
intro.cn: notary 建立在拉丁语「标记」词族上：nota、notare、notarius，英语里又造出 notarial 与 notarize。

latinIntro.en: Latin nota means a mark, notare means to mark, and notarius is the clerk who writes marks.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nota 意为记号，notare 意为作标记，notarius 是写下记号的书记。

items.example: Nota gives the family its core image of a mark.
items.exampleCN: nota 给这个词族提供「标记」的核心意象。

items.example: Notare turns the mark into an act of writing.
items.exampleCN: notare 把记号变成写作的动作。

items.example: Notarius is the person behind the office.
items.exampleCN: notarius 就是这一职务背后的人。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms person nouns from stems.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ary 从词干构成指人的名词。

items.example: Notary is the shortened everyday title.
items.exampleCN: notary 是日常使用的简称。

items.example: Notarial describes acts done before a notary.
items.exampleCN: notarial 描述在公证人面前完成的行为。

items.example: Notarize turns the office into an action.
items.exampleCN: notarize 把这一职务变成一个动作。

items.example: Notarization names the completed procedure.
items.exampleCN: notarization 指完成后的公证手续。

items.example: Notarized marks a document as already certified.
items.exampleCN: notarized 标记一份文书已经公证。

definition_zh: 笔记；便条；音符；注意；记下
definition_en: a short written record or message; a single musical sound; attention; and the act of noticing or writing something down
core_image: 纸页边缘写满小字，一张折好的短笺压在书页之间
scene: 厨房的桌上压着一张折好的纸条，字迹很急，末尾没有署名。She read the note twice before answering.
sceneCN: 这里是「便条、短笺」（第 2 个义项：写在纸上的简短留言），句意为她把那张便条读了两遍才回话。图中可辨识物件：折好的纸条、厨房桌、笔。

derivatives.zh: 由 note 与 book 复合而成，义为「笔记本」
由 note 的拉丁词干加 -able 构成，义为「值得注意的；显著的」
由拉丁词干 notare 加 -tion 构成，义为「记号系统；记谱法」

senses.title: A short written record of something heard or read
senses.definition: a short written record, especially of what a speaker said or what a reader wants to remember
senses.definitionCN: 简短的书面记录，尤指记下讲者所说或读者想记住的内容
senses.example: She filled three pages with notes during the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座期间她记满了三页笔记。
senses.why: Latin nota was a mark or written sign, and the first English sense kept that idea of a small written trace left behind for later use.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nota 是「记号、写下的符号」，英语最初的意思保留了这种「为以后使用而留下的小小书写痕迹」。

senses.title: A short written message
senses.definition: a short informal letter or message written on a piece of paper
senses.definitionCN: 写在纸上的简短、非正式的留言或信
senses.example: She read the note twice before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那张便条读了两遍才回话。
senses.why: Because any written mark can be handed to someone else, note slid from a private record to a message left for another person, usually brief and casual.
senses.whyCN: 既然任何书写记号都能交给别人，note 就从私人记录滑向留给别人的留言，通常简短而随意。

senses.title: A single musical sound or its written sign
senses.definition: a single sound in music, or the written symbol that stands for it
senses.definitionCN: 音乐中的单个音，或代表这个音的书写符号
senses.example: She held the last note longer than the others.
senses.exampleCN: 她把最后一个音拖得比别的音更长。
senses.why: A musical tone can be written down like any other sign, so the word for a written mark came to name one printed dot on a staff and then the sound it stands for.
senses.whyCN: 乐音也能像别的符号一样写下来，于是表示书写记号的词先指谱线中的一个点，再指它所代表的那个音。

senses.title: Attention or notice given to something
senses.definition: attention given to something, especially in the phrase take note of
senses.definitionCN: 对某事给予的关注，尤用于 take note of 这一说法
senses.example: Take note of the small changes in the pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 请留意这个图案里细微的变化。
senses.why: A note is something you write so that it will be remembered, and from that comes the sense of giving something enough attention for it to be remembered.
senses.whyCN: 笔记是为了日后记得才写下的东西，由此引申出「给予足够关注、以便记住」的意思。

senses.title: To notice or write something down
senses.definition: to notice something and give it attention, or to write it down so that it is recorded
senses.definitionCN: 注意到某事并加以关注，或把它写下来留作记录
senses.example: He noted the time in the margin of his notebook.
senses.exampleCN: 他把时间记在笔记本的页边。
senses.why: Once the noun means a written trace of attention, the matching verb naturally means the act that produces it, so noting is both watching closely and setting the result on paper.
senses.whyCN: 当名词已经表示「注意力留下的书写痕迹」，与之对应的动词自然就表示产生这个痕迹的动作，所以 noting 既是仔细观察，也是把结果落到纸上。

intro.en: Note comes from a Latin word for a mark or written sign, entered English through Old French, and later grew senses for messages, music and attention.
intro.cn: note 来自拉丁语中表示「记号、书写符号」的词，经古法语进入英语，后来才长出留言、音乐与注意等义项。

items.en: Nota was a mark, a written character or a sign of something, and it is generally connected with the Latin verb for knowing, noscere.
items.cn: nota 是记号、书写符号或某事的标志，一般认为它与拉丁语中表示「认识」的动词 noscere 有关。

items.en: The verb notare meant to mark, to write down or to observe, and it supplied the family of words about noting and notation.
items.cn: 动词 notare 意为标记、写下或观察，由此衍生出与记录和记号系统有关的一族词。

items.en: Old French passed on note as a written mark, a memorandum or a short writing after the Norman period.
items.cn: 诺曼时期之后，古法语把 note 传进英语，意思为书面的记号、备忘或短小的文字。

items.en: Middle English note covered a written record, a melody and a token of something, so the musical sense was already present.
items.cn: 中古英语的 note 已包含书面记录、曲调与某事物的标志，音乐义那时就已经在场。

items.en: Modern English adds the short message, the musical symbol, the sense of attention and the verb, together with the compound banknote for paper money.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了便条、音乐符号、注意等意思和动词用法，还添上表示纸币的复合词 banknote。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem nota through English derivatives; the near-meaning group collects the short writings and messages that note resembles.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁词干 nota 收英语派生词；近义组收与 note 相近的短小文字与留言。

entries.definition: A system of written symbols, such as the notation used for music.
entries.definitionCN: 书写符号的系统，如音乐所用的记谱法。

entries.definition: Worthy of attention, built from the same stem with -able.
entries.definitionCN: 值得注意的，同一词干加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: A book of blank pages for writing notes.
entries.definitionCN: 用来记笔记、带空白页的本子。

entries.definition: A short written message inside an office or organization.
entries.definitionCN: 办公室或机构内部简短的书面留言。

entries.definition: Information sent from one person to another, in speech, writing or another medium.
entries.definitionCN: 由一人传给另一人的信息，可用口头、书面或其他方式。

entries.definition: A written or stored account of something kept for later reference.
entries.definitionCN: 为日后查阅而保存的书面或存储记载。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin mark that became a small piece of writing, then a message, a musical sign and a act of attention.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词原是拉丁语的「记号」，后来变成一小段文字、一条留言、一个音乐符号，以及一次关注的动作。

normal.en: Latin nota meant a mark or written sign, so every sense of note still involves something set down to be seen again.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nota 意为记号或书写符号，所以 note 的每个义项都离不开「写下来以便再看」这件事。

normal.en: Notare is the Latin verb to mark or write, and it is the base of notation and notable.
normal.cn: notare 是拉丁语里「标记、书写」的动词，也是 notation 与 notable 的底座。

normal.en: The musical note is simply a written sign on a staff, which is why the same word names the symbol and the sound.
normal.cn: 音乐里的 note 不过是谱线上的一个书写符号，所以同一个词既指符号也指声音。

normal.en: Take note of keeps the physical picture: you write something because you want to keep it in mind.
normal.cn: take note of 保留了那个具体画面：你把它写下来，是因为想把它记在心里。

normal.en: Banknote is a note in the old sense of a written promise to pay, now the paper money itself.
normal.cn: banknote 里的 note 用的是旧义「书面的付款承诺」，今天则直接指那张纸币。

abstract.en: A mark that was meant to be read later became a message meant for someone else, and both still depend on paper holding a thought still.
abstract.cn: 一个本来留给以后自己看的记号，变成了留给别人的留言，两者都依赖纸张把一个念头固定住。

abstract.en: Note shows how writing turns attention into an object: what you noticed becomes something you can hand over.
abstract.cn: note 展示了书写如何把注意力变成物件：你注意到的东西变成可以递交出去的东西。

abstract.en: The same short word can be a page of study, a line of music and a warning, because all three are traces left for a later reader.
abstract.cn: 同一个短词可以是整页的学习、一行音乐，也可以是一句提醒，因为三者都是留给后来读者看的痕迹。

examples.en: She read the note twice before answering.
examples.cn: 她把那张便条读了两遍才回话。

examples.en: She filled three pages with notes during the lecture.
examples.cn: 讲座期间她记满了三页笔记。

examples.en: He noted the time in the margin of his notebook.
examples.cn: 他把时间记在笔记本的页边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺特」——桌上压着一张小纸条，几行字就说明了来意；note 就是便条、笔记。

root: 拉丁语 nota（记号、书写符号）与动词 notare（标记、写下），经古法语 note 进入中古英语；同族词有 notable、notation、notebook。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a written mark kept for later; the senses then divide into the record, the message, the musical sign, and attention with its verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「为日后而留下的书写记号」；义项由此分出记录、留言、音乐符号，以及注意和相应的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page crowded with small handwriting, with a folded slip pressed between the leaves.
core.cn: 核心意象：写满小字的纸页，夹着一张折好的短笺。

branches.en: a page of lecture notes written in a tight hand
branches.cn: 写得密密麻麻的一页讲座笔记

branches.en: a sentence underlined twice in the margin
branches.cn: 页边被划了两道线的句子

branches.en: a folded slip left on a kitchen table
branches.cn: 厨房桌上留下的折好的纸条

branches.en: one held tone at the end of a song
branches.cn: 歌曲结尾一个被拖长的音

branches.en: a reader pausing, then writing a date in the corner
branches.cn: 读者停了一下，在角上写下日期

intro.cn: 这个词立在拉丁语表示「记号」的名词与动词上，再由英语词尾构成它的派生词与复合词。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 nota 与动词 notare 是这个词族有记录的来源，因此下面的拉丁词条是它的直系祖先。

definition_zh: 明显的；显而易见的；显著的；显眼的
definition_en: easy to see or notice, and large or important enough to attract attention
core_image: 白墙上一道新刷的痕迹，走过的人都忍不住多看两眼
scene: 换上新窗帘的那个下午，屋里一下子亮了许多，来串门的邻居刚进门就停住脚步。The change in the room was noticeable the moment the door opened.
sceneCN: 这里 noticeable 是「看得出来的、明显的」（第 1 个义项：容易被人察觉）；句意为门一开，屋里的变化就一眼可见。图中可辨识物件：新窗帘、亮起来的窗、停在门口的邻居。

pos.zh: 明显的；显而易见的；显著的；显眼的

derivatives.zh: 由 noticeable 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「明显地」
由否定前缀 un- 加 noticeable 构成，义为「察觉不到的」

senses.title: Easily seen or heard
senses.definition: possible to see, hear or feel without much effort
senses.definitionCN: 不用费多大劲就能看见、听见或感觉到
senses.example: There was a noticeable gap between the two shelves.
senses.exampleCN: 两层架子之间有一道明显的缝隙。
senses.why: The suffix -able marks what can be done to something, so noticeable literally means able to be noticed; the adjective begins with the eye's power to catch a thing.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 标出「能被施加某动作」的性质，所以 noticeable 字面就是「能被注意到的」；这个形容词的起点，是眼睛捕捉东西的能力。

senses.title: Large enough to matter or to be measured
senses.definition: great enough in size or effect to deserve attention
senses.definitionCN: 在程度、数量或效果上大到值得关注
senses.example: The new drug produced a noticeable drop in blood pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 新药让血压出现了明显下降。
senses.why: Once a thing can be noticed, the word can also measure how much it deserves to be noticed, so the sense slides from visibility to degree and importance.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西既然能被注意到，这个词也就能衡量它值多少注意力，于是词义从「看得见」滑向「程度与分量」。

senses.title: Attracting attention by appearance
senses.definition: drawing people's eyes because of how a person or thing looks
senses.definitionCN: 因为外表而不断招来别人的目光
senses.example: In a crowd of grey coats her red scarf was noticeable.
senses.exampleCN: 在一群灰外套里，她的红围巾很显眼。
senses.why: A person or object that keeps pulling eyes is the same visible quality turned outward, which is how the adjective comes to mean standing out in a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 老是把人目光拉过去的人或物，是同一份「可见性」向外翻了出来，形容词因此多出「在人群中出挑」的意思。

intro.en: The adjective is a Latin-rooted English noun fitted with an English suffix; notice supplies the idea of being known and -able turns it into a quality.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是一个带拉丁词根的英语名词接上英语后缀：notice 提供「被知道」的观念，-able 把它变成一种性质。

items.en: The verb noscere, to get to know, gave notice its earliest idea of something becoming known.
items.cn: 动词 noscere 意为认识，给了 notice 最初的观念：某样东西被知道了。

items.en: Notitia, the state of being known, reached French as notice and then passed into English as a noun.
items.cn: notitia 表示「被知道的状态」，到法语写作 notice，再以名词进入英语。

items.en: By the sixteenth century English already had notice as a familiar noun for information and warning.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，英语里的 notice 已是表示消息与警告的常用名词。

items.en: The suffix -able, from Latin -abilis, was freely added to English verbs and nouns to mean able to be.
items.cn: 后缀 -able 源自拉丁语 -abilis，在英语中可自由加在动词和名词后，表示「能被……的」。

items.en: Noticeable settled in the eighteenth century and later gained the sense of a size or effect large enough to deserve attention.
items.cn: noticeable 在十八世纪定型，后来又添上「程度或效果大到值得注意」的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on notice; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for what is easy to see.
note.cn: 形近组收由 notice 构成的各种形态；近义组收表示「容易看见」的形容词。

entries.definition: In a way that is easy to see or notice.
entries.definitionCN: 以容易看见或察觉的方式。

entries.definition: So slight or well hidden that it cannot be noticed.
entries.definitionCN: 细微或隐蔽到无法被察觉的。

entries.definition: The noun and verb from which this adjective is built.
entries.definitionCN: 构成这个形容词的名词与动词。

entries.definition: So clear that no explanation is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 清楚到不需要解释的。

entries.definition: Clearly shown by facts or signs.
entries.definitionCN: 由事实或迹象清楚显示的。

entries.definition: Very easy to see, often because of size or colour.
entries.definitionCN: 因大小或颜色而非常显眼的。

entries.definition: Just strong enough to be felt by the senses.
entries.definitionCN: 强度刚够被感官觉察的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a plain sum: notice plus -able, with the suffix doing nothing more than turning a pair of eyes into a quality of the thing seen.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一次直白的相加：notice 加 -able，后缀只做一件事——把一双眼睛变成被看之物身上的性质。

normal.en: Noticeable is notice plus -able, meaning able to be noticed, and the final e of notice stays before the suffix.
normal.cn: noticeable 是 notice 加 -able，意为「能被注意到的」，notice 词尾的 e 在加后缀时保留。

normal.en: The same -able appears in readable, drinkable and washable, all meaning able to be read, drunk or washed.
normal.cn: 同一个 -able 也出现在 readable、drinkable、washable 里，都表示「能被读、喝、洗」。

normal.en: The negative is unnoticeable, with un- in front, meaning not able to be noticed at all.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 unnoticeable，前面加 un-，意为根本察觉不到。

normal.en: The adverb noticeably drops the final e and adds -ly, naming the manner in which something is seen.
normal.cn: 副词 noticeably 去掉词尾 e 再加 -ly，指某物被看见的方式。

normal.en: Noticeable difference is the everyday pairing, because the word measures how far two things stand apart.
normal.cn: noticeable difference 是最常见的搭配，因为这个词衡量的就是两样东西差得多远。

abstract.en: A change becomes noticeable at the moment someone else's eyes confirm what you already felt.
abstract.cn: 变化在别人的眼睛替你确认的那一刻，才算明显。

abstract.en: The suffix -able quietly turns a pair of eyes into a quality of the thing being looked at.
abstract.cn: 后缀 -able 悄悄把一双眼睛，变成了被看之物身上的一种性质。

abstract.en: What is noticeable is not only seen but weighed: the word asks how much attention a thing deserves.
abstract.cn: 明显的东西不只被看见，还被掂量：这个词在问一样东西值多少注意力。

examples.en: There was a noticeable gap between the two shelves.
examples.cn: 两层架子之间有一道明显的缝隙。

examples.en: The new paint made a noticeable difference to the hallway.
examples.cn: 新刷的漆让门厅明显不一样了。

examples.en: Her red scarf was noticeable in the grey crowd.
examples.cn: 在灰扑扑的人群里，她的红围巾很显眼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺替色波」——那块颜色扎眼得像块色布，走过的人都要看一眼；noticeable 就是明显的。

root: 由 notice（注意到）加形容词后缀 -able 构成；notice 一般认为来自拉丁语 notitia，源于 noscere（认识）。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective takes the noun's idea of being known and turns it into a quality: whatever can be caught by the eye, then whatever is large enough to matter, then whatever stands out in a crowd.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词把名词「被知道」的观念变成一种性质：先是能被眼睛捕捉，再是大到有分量，最后是在人群中出挑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fresh mark on a white wall that makes every passer-by look twice.
core.cn: 核心意象：白墙上的一道新痕，让每个路过的人都多看两眼。

branches.en: a gap between shelves the eye finds at once
branches.cn: 一眼就看见的架子缝隙

branches.en: a new curtain changing the light in a room
branches.cn: 新窗帘改变了屋里的光

branches.en: a test score rising by a clear margin
branches.cn: 考试成绩抬升了明显的一截

branches.en: a red scarf in a crowd of grey coats
branches.cn: 灰衣人群里的红围巾

branches.en: a change big enough to be talked about
branches.cn: 大到会被人议论的变化

intro.en: The adjective is a Latin-rooted noun joined to an English suffix, so its structure is as simple as it looks: notice plus -able.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是拉丁词根的名词接上一个英语后缀，结构看上去有多简单就有多简单：notice 加 -able。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 通知；告知；申报；报备；推送通知
definition_en: to tell someone something officially, especially in writing, and to report a fact to an authority
core_image: 一封封好的信，被递到那个必须知道的人手里
scene: 护照到期之前，窗口里的工作人员把一封打印好的信推到申请人面前，请他核对地址后签字。The bank notified every customer of the new fee in writing.
sceneCN: 这里 notify 是「正式通知、告知」（第 1 个义项：把消息正式送到某人手里）；句意为银行用书面形式把新收费告知每位客户。图中可辨识物件：办事窗口、打印的信、签字笔。

derivatives.zh: 由 notify 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「通知；通告」
由 notify 加表「做某事的人或物」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「通知者；通知程序」
由 notify 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「须上报的」

senses.title: To tell someone something officially
senses.definition: to give someone information in an official or formal way
senses.definitionCN: 以官方或正式的方式把消息告诉某人
senses.example: Please notify us of any change in your contact details.
senses.exampleCN: 联系方式若有变动，请通知我们。
senses.why: Notus means known and -ify means to make, so notify is literally to make something known; its force sits on the telling, not on the seeing.
senses.whyCN: notus 意为「已知的」，-ify 意为「使」，所以 notify 字面就是「使某事被知道」；它的着力点在「告诉」，而不在「看见」。

senses.title: To report a fact to an authority
senses.definition: to report something to an official body because a rule requires it
senses.definitionCN: 因规定要求而把事情报告给官方机构
senses.example: All new cases must be notified to the health department.
senses.exampleCN: 所有新病例都必须上报卫生部门。
senses.why: The same making-known turns into a duty when a rule demands it, so the verb picks up the legal sense of filing a report with an office.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「使被知道」，一旦有规定要求，就变成一种义务，动词于是添上「向机关报备」的法律含义。

senses.title: Of software, to send a message to a user
senses.definition: to have a program send a message that appears on a user's screen
senses.definitionCN: 由程序发出消息，显示在用户屏幕上
senses.example: The app notifies you when your train is delayed.
senses.exampleCN: 列车晚点时，这款应用会推送提醒。
senses.why: A machine now does the telling, so the verb extends from people to software that makes a message known on a screen.
senses.whyCN: 如今由机器来完成告知，动词便从人扩展到软件：把一条消息呈现在屏幕上让人知道。

intro.en: Notify is a Latin compound meaning to make known: a participle for known joined to a verb of making, carried into English through French.
intro.cn: notify 是一个意为「使被知道」的拉丁语复合词：表示「已知」的分词接上一个表示「制作」的动词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Noscere, to get to know, supplied the family with its participle notus, meaning known.
items.cn: noscere 意为认识，为这个词族提供了分词 notus，意为「已知的」。

items.en: Facere meant to make or to do, and it supplied the -ficare ending used in verbs of making.
items.cn: facere 意为制作、做，提供了动词中常见的词尾 -ficare。

items.en: Medieval Latin joined the two into notificare, to make known, a word at home in documents and official acts.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语把两者合成 notificare，意为「使被知道」，是文书与官方行为里的常用词。

items.en: Old French notifier carried that official flavour into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 notifier 带着这份官方色彩，在诺曼时期之后进入英语。

items.en: Modern English keeps the official tone, adds the legal sense of reporting to authorities, and now lets software notify its users.
items.cn: 现代英语保留官方语气，添上向主管部门报备的法律义，如今又让软件向用户推送通知。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family derived from this verb; the near-meaning group collects verbs for passing information.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个动词派生的同族词；近义组收表示传递信息的动词。

entries.definition: A message that officially tells someone something.
entries.definitionCN: 正式告知某人的一条消息。

entries.definition: A person or program that sends a notification.
entries.definitionCN: 发出通知的人或程序。

entries.definition: Required by law to be reported to an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 法律规定必须向主管部门报告的。

entries.definition: To tell someone facts they did not have.
entries.definitionCN: 把对方尚不知道的事实告知。

entries.definition: To warn someone about something urgent.
entries.definitionCN: 就紧急之事提醒某人。

entries.definition: To make something public to many people at once.
entries.definitionCN: 当众公开宣布某事。

entries.definition: To give information to someone in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 用言语把信息告诉某人。

normalIntro.en: The verb is a Latin sum of known plus make, so every use of it contains someone who must be told and something that must become known.
normalIntro.cn: 这个动词是拉丁语的「已知」加「使」，所以它每次出现，都含着一个必须被告诉的人和一桩必须被知道的事。

normal.en: Notus means known and -ify means to make, so notify is to make known, which is why it always needs someone to receive the message.
normal.cn: notus 意为已知，-ify 意为使，所以 notify 就是「使被知道」；也正因如此，它总需要一个收消息的人。

normal.en: The frame notify someone of something is standard, with of marking what the message is about.
normal.cn: notify someone of something 是标准句式，of 后面标出消息的内容。

normal.en: Notice comes from the noun notitia and centres on seeing; notify comes from notificare and centres on telling. A glance notices, an office notifies.
normal.cn: notice 出自名词 notitia，重心在看见；notify 出自 notificare，重心在告知。眼睛可以 notice，机关则要 notify。

normal.en: Notification adds -ation to the verb, naming the message that arrives rather than the act of sending it.
normal.cn: notification 在动词后加 -ation，指送达的那条消息，而不是发送这个动作。

normal.en: In law notifiable diseases must be reported, so the adjective carries an obligation that the verb alone does not.
normal.cn: 在法律里 notifiable disease 必须上报，这个形容词带着动词本身所没有的义务。

abstract.en: Notice is what your eyes do; notify is what an office does with a stamp.
abstract.cn: notice 是眼睛做的事；notify 是机构盖章做的事。

abstract.en: Every notification is a small claim that someone out there needs to know.
abstract.cn: 每一条通知都是一个轻微的断言：外面有人需要知道这件事。

abstract.en: A word that once meant simply making known now runs through paper letters and phone screens without changing its core.
abstract.cn: 一个曾经只表示「使被知道」的词，如今穿行于纸质信件与手机屏幕，核心却没有变。

examples.en: The bank notified every customer of the new fee.
examples.cn: 银行把新收费告知了每位客户。

examples.en: You must notify the authorities within ten days of moving.
examples.cn: 搬家后十天之内必须向主管部门报备。

examples.en: The app notifies you when your train is delayed.
examples.cn: 列车晚点时，这款应用会推送提醒。
